22:1: Surat Al-Hajj In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty says, commanding His servants to fear Him and informing them of the horrors, earthquakes and conditions that await them on the Day of Resurrection. The commentators differed about the earthquake of the Hour: Will it be after people rise from their graves on the Day of Resurrection, or will it be an expression for the earthquake of the earth before people rise from their graves? As God the Almighty said: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, And the earth discharges its burdens. And God the Almighty said: “And the earth and the mountains will be lifted up and crushed with a single blow. On that Day the Inevitable will occur.” And God the Almighty said: When the earth is shaken with a [final] earthquake, And the mountains are crushed with a [final] destruction. Some say: This earthquake will occur at the end of the world and the beginning of the conditions of the Hour. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, regarding his statement: Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing, he said: Before the Hour. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Thawri, on the authority of Mansur and Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, and he mentioned it. He said: Something similar was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim, and Ubayd ibn Umair. Abu Kudaynah said on the authority of Ata’ ibn Amir Al-Sha’bi: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing,” he said: This is in this world before the Day of Resurrection. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir cited the evidence of those who said that in the hadith of the images from the narration of Ismail bin Rafi’, the judge of the people of Medina, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the image and gave it to Israfil, who is placing it on his mouth, staring at the Throne, waiting for when he will be commanded. Abu Hurairah said: O Messenger of God, what is the image? He said: A horn. He said: What is it like? He said: “A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of stun, and the third is the blast of rising before the Lord of the Worlds. God will command Israfil to blow the first blast. He will say: Blow the blast of terror, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will be terrified except for whom God wills. He will command him to extend it and prolong it and not cease. It is the one about which God the Most High says: “And these do not await except a single blast that will have no end.” So he will cover the mountains and they will become a mirage, and the earth will shake with its inhabitants with a violent shaking. It is the one about which God the Most High says: The Day when the great earthquake will shake, followed by the second earthquake, hearts that Day will be trembling. So the earth will be like a ship that is destroyed in the sea, struck by waves that will overturn it and its inhabitants, and like a lantern suspended from the throne, rocked by the spirits, and people will stretch out on its back, so nursing mothers will be stunned and pregnant women will give birth, and children will turn gray, and the devils will fly away until they reach the regions and the angels will meet them and strike them in the faces and they will turn back, and the people will turn away.” They will call out to one another, and this is what God the Almighty says: “The Day of Calling * The Day you will turn back, departing. You will have no protector from God. And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no guide.” While they were in that state, the earth split open from one region to another, and they saw a great matter, and they were seized by that from distress, which God knows best. Then they looked at the sky and saw it as molten metal, then its sun and moon were eclipsed, and its stars were scattered and then removed from them. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: And the dead do not know anything about that. Abu Hurairah said: So who excepted God when He says: So whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills, he said: “Those are the witnesses, and the terror only reaches the living. They are alive with their Lord, provided for. God protected them from the evil of that Day and made them safe. It is the punishment of God that He sends upon the worst of His creation, and it is what God says: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget what she was nursing, and she will give birth.” Every being will bear its burden, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe.” This hadith was narrated by al-Tabarani, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and others at great length. The purpose of it is that it indicates that this earthquake will occur before the Day of Resurrection, and it was added to the Hour because of its proximity to it, just as it is said, Signs of the Hour and the like. And God knows best. Others said, Rather, it is terror, panic, earthquake, and confusion that will occur on the Day of Resurrection in the places of assembly after rising from the graves. Ibn Jarir chose this, and they provided evidence with hadiths: First Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Hisham, Qatada told us on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Imran bin Husayn that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while he was on one of his journeys, and the distances of his companions varied, he raised his voice with these two verses. “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her suckling, and every pregnant female will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they will not be drunk. Rather, the punishment of God is severe.” When his companions heard that, they urged their mounts on, and they knew that he was about to say something. When they drew near to him, he said, “Do you know what day that is? That is the day when Adam, peace be upon him, will be called out to his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and He will say, ‘O Adam, send your people to the Fire. ’ He will say, ‘O Lord, what are the people sent to the Fire? ’ He will say, ‘Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine will be in the Fire and one will be in Paradise. ’ His companions were so dazed that they could hardly even laugh. When he saw that, he said, ‘Be glad and work, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creatures who have never been with anything except that they increased it: Gog and Magog, and those who perished from the children of Adam and the children of Iblis. ’ He said, ‘So their sorrow was relieved, then he said, ‘Work and be glad, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creatures who have never been with anything except that they increased it. Gog and Magog, and those who perished from the children of Adam and the children of Iblis. ’ He said, ‘So their sorrow was relieved, and he said, ‘Work and be glad, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are with two creatures who have never been with anything except that they increased it. ’ Muhammad’s soul is in His hand. You are among people like a mole on the side of a camel or a mark on the arm of an animal.” And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in the Book of Interpretation of their Sunan on the authority of Muhammad bin Bashar on the authority of Yahya, who is Al-Qattan, on the authority of Hisham, who is Al-Dastawa’i, on the authority of Qatadah, with a similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. Another way to this hadith. Al-Tirmidhi said: Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, Ibn Jud’an told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran ibn Husayn, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when the verse was revealed: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing. The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her suckling, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy, and you will see the people as if they were drunk, but they are not drunk. Rather, the punishment of God is severe.” He said: This verse was revealed to him while he was on a journey, so he said: Do you know what day that is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “That is the day when God will say to Adam: ‘Send those sent to Hellfire.’ He said: “O Lord, what are those sent to Hellfire?” He said: Nine hundred and ninety-nine to Hellfire and one to Paradise. The Muslims began to cry, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come close and aim straight, for there has never been a prophethood except that there was ignorance before it. He said: “The number will be taken from the ignorance, and if it is complete, then it will be completed by the hypocrites. And the likeness of you and the nations is not like that except that there is no difference between you and the hypocrites.” Like a mark on the arm of an animal or like a mole on the side of a camel. Then he said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise - so they said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise - so they said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise - so they said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I do not know whether he said two-thirds or not. And Imam Ahmad narrated it in the same way on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah. Then al-Tirmidhi also said: This is a hasan saheeh hadeeth. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Imran bin Al-Hussain. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Arubah on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Al-Hasan and Al-Ala bin Ziyad Al-Adawi on the authority of Imran bin Al-Hussain, and he mentioned it. And Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Aouf on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Al-Usrah with his companions after he approached Madinah, he recited: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing.” And he mentioned the hadith, and he mentioned something similar to the context of Ibn Jud’an, and God knows best. The second hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn al-Tabba’ told us, Abu Sufyan al-Ma’mari told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing was revealed, and he mentioned, meaning something similar to the context of al-Hasan on the authority of Imran, except that he said: And whoever perishes because of the great number of jinn and mankind. Ibn Jarir narrated it in full from the hadith of Muammar. The third hadith Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Saeed bin Salman told us, Ibad told us, meaning Ibn Al-Awwam told us, Hilal bin Khabab told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse and mentioned something similar to it, and said in it: “I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise - then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise - then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise, so rejoice.” He also added: And you are only a part of a thousand parts. Hadith 4 Al-Bukhari said when interpreting this verse: Umar ibn Hafs told us, my father told us, Al-A’mash told us, Abu Salih told us on the authority of Abu Sa’id who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, God Almighty will say: O Adam! He will say: At your service, our Lord, and at your pleasure! Then a voice will call out: God commands you to send forth from your offspring a group to the Fire. He will say: O Lord, and what are the groups to the Fire? He will say: From every thousand - I think he said - nine hundred and ninety-nine. Then the pregnant woman will give birth to her burden and the newborn will turn white. “And you will see the people drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe.” This was difficult for the people until their faces changed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “From Gog and Magog, nine hundred and ninety-nine, and from you is one. You are among the people like a black hair on the side of a white bull, or like a white hair on the side of a black bull. I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise - so we said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: A third of the people of Paradise - so we said Allahu Akbar. Then he said: “The people of Paradise are divided” so we woke up early. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in a place other than this, and Muslim and Al-Nasa’i in his interpretation from various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. The fifth hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ammarah bin Muhammad, the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ubaydah al-Ma’ni told us, both on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, God will send a caller who will call out: ‘O Adam, God commands you to send a group of your descendants to the Fire.’ Adam will say: ‘O Lord, who are they?’ It will be said to him: ‘Out of every hundred, ninety-nine.’ A man from the people will say: ‘Who among us will be saved after this, O Messenger of God?’ He will say: ‘Do you know that you are among people like a mole on the chest of a camel?’” This chain of transmission and this context is unique to Imam Ahmad. The sixth hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Hatim bin Abi Safira, Ibn Abi Malekah told us that Al-Qasim bin Muhammad told him on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will be gathered before God on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. Aisha said: O Messenger of God, men and women will look at each other. He said: O Aisha, the matter is more serious than that for them to be concerned about. They included it in the two Sahihs. The Seventh Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, will the beloved remember his beloved on the Day of Resurrection? He said: O Aisha, as for three things, no. As for the scales until they become heavy or light, no. As for when the books fly apart, either he will be given with his right hand or he will be given with his left hand, no. And when a neck emerges from the Fire, it will fold over them and become angry with them, and that neck will say: I am entrusted with three, I am entrusted with three, I am entrusted with three. I am entrusted with those who claim another god with God, and I am entrusted with those who do not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and I am entrusted with every stubborn tyrant - he said - so it will fold over them and throw them into the depths of Hell. And Hell has a bridge thinner than hair and sharper than a sword, on which are hooks and thorns that seize whomever God wills, and the people on it are like lightning, like a flash, like the wind, and like the best horses and riders, and the angels say: O Lord, save us, save us.” A Muslim is saved, a Muslim is scratched, and he is curled up in the fire on his face. The hadiths and reports on the horrors of the Day of Resurrection are very numerous and have another place. That is why God Almighty said: The earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing. That is, a great matter, a serious matter, a terrifying intruder, a terrible event, and a strange occurrence. The earthquake is what happens to the souls of terror and fear, as God Almighty said: There the believers will be tested and shaken with a severe earthquake. Then God Almighty said: On the Day you see it. This is from the perspective of the pronoun of the matter. That is why He explained it by saying: Every nursing mother will forget what she nursed. That is, she will be preoccupied with the horror of what she sees and will forget the person dearest to her, and the one who is most compassionate towards him will forget about him while she is nursing him. That is why He said: Every nursing mother, and He did not say nurse. He said: What she nursed, meaning about her infant before he is weaned. And His saying: And every pregnant female will abort her pregnancy meaning before its completion due to the intensity of the terror. And you will see the people drunk. It was read drunk meaning from the intensity of the matter in which they have become, their minds have been astonished and their thoughts have become absent, so whoever sees them will think that they are drunk. But they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe.

Al-Bukhari also narrated it in a place other than this, and Muslim and Al-Nasa’i in his interpretation from various chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash. The fifth hadith Imam Ahmad said: Ammarah bin Muhammad, the nephew of Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ubaydah al-Ma’ni told us, both on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muslim, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, God will send a caller who will call out: ‘O Adam, God commands you to send a group of your descendants to the Fire.’ Adam will say: ‘O Lord, who are they?’ It will be said to him: ‘Out of every hundred, ninety-nine.’ A man from the people will say: ‘Who among us will be saved after this, O Messenger of God?’ He will say: ‘Do you know that you are among people like a mole on the chest of a camel?’” This chain of transmission and this context is unique to Imam Ahmad. The sixth hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Hatim bin Abi Safira, Ibn Abi Malekah told us that Al-Qasim bin Muhammad told him on the authority of Aisha on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will be gathered before God on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. Aisha said: O Messenger of God, men and women will look at each other. He said: O Aisha, the matter is more serious than that for them to be concerned about. They included it in the two Sahihs. The Seventh Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “I said, O Messenger of God, will the beloved remember his beloved on the Day of Resurrection? He said: O Aisha, as for three things, no. As for the scales until they become heavy or light, no. As for when the books fly apart, either he will be given with his right hand or he will be given with his left hand, no. And when a neck emerges from the Fire, it will fold over them and become angry with them, and that neck will say: I am entrusted with three, I am entrusted with three, I am entrusted with three. I am entrusted with those who claim another god with God, and I am entrusted with those who do not believe in the Day of Reckoning, and I am entrusted with every stubborn tyrant - he said - so it will fold over them and throw them into the depths of Hell. And Hell has a bridge thinner than hair and sharper than a sword, on which are hooks and thorns that seize whomever God wills, and the people on it are like lightning, like a flash, like the wind, and like the best horses and riders, and the angels say: O Lord, save us, save us.” A Muslim is saved, a Muslim is scratched, and he is curled up in the fire on his face. The hadiths and reports on the horrors of the Day of Resurrection are very numerous and have another place. That is why God Almighty said: The earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing. That is, a great matter, a serious matter, a terrifying intruder, a terrible event, and a strange occurrence. The earthquake is what happens to the souls of terror and fear, as God Almighty said: There the believers will be tested and shaken with a severe earthquake. Then God Almighty said: On the Day you see it. This is from the perspective of the pronoun of the matter. That is why He explained it by saying: Every nursing mother will forget what she nursed. That is, she will be preoccupied with the horror of what she sees and will forget the person dearest to her, and the one who is most compassionate towards him will forget about him while she is nursing him. That is why He said: Every nursing mother, and He did not say nurse. He said: What she nursed, meaning about her infant before he is weaned. And His saying: And every pregnant female will abort her pregnancy meaning before its completion due to the intensity of the terror. And you will see the people drunk. It was read drunk meaning from the intensity of the matter in which they have become, their minds have been astonished and their thoughts have become absent, so whoever sees them will think that they are drunk. But they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe.
22:3: God Almighty says, blaming those who deny the resurrection and reject the ability of God to revive the dead, turning away from what God revealed to His prophets, following in their words, denial and disbelief every rebellious devil from mankind and jinn. This is the state of the people of innovation and misguidance who turn away from the truth and follow falsehood. They abandon what God revealed to His Messenger of the clear truth, and follow the sayings of the leaders of misguidance who call to innovations with whims and opinions. For this reason, He said about them and their likes: And among mankind is he who disputes about God without knowledge meaning correct knowledge “and follows every rebellious devil. It is written for him” Mujahid said: He means the devil, meaning it is written for him a decree of destiny that whoever takes him as a friend meaning follows him and imitates him he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze meaning he will mislead him in this world, and lead him in the Hereafter to the punishment of the Blaze, which is the hot, painful, disturbing and disturbing. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Abu Malik: This verse was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and Ibn Jurayj said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Muslim al-Basri told us, Amr ibn al-Muharram Abu Qatada told us, al-Umar told us, Abu Kaab al-Makki told us: An evil man from the evil ones of Quraysh said: Tell us about your Lord, is He made of gold, or of silver, or of copper? Then the sky rumbled - and the rumble in the speech of the Arabs means thunder - and behold, his head fell down before him. Layth ibn Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid: A Jew came and said: O Muhammad, tell me about your Lord, what is He made of - pearls or rubies? He said: Then a thunderbolt came and took him.

22:5: When the Almighty mentioned the one who opposes the resurrection and denies the afterlife, the Almighty mentioned the evidence of His Almighty power over the afterlife, as seen from His beginning of creation, saying: O mankind, if you are in doubt meaning in doubt about the resurrection which is the afterlife, and the rising of souls and bodies on the Day of Resurrection then We created you from dust meaning an origin that He created for you from dust, which is what He created Adam, peace be upon him, from then from a sperm-drop meaning then He made his offspring from a lineage of despised water then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh that is, when the sperm settles in the womb of the woman, it remains for forty days like this, and whatever is collected in it is added to it, then it turns into a red clot by the permission of God, and it remains like this for forty days, then it is transformed and becomes a lump of flesh, a piece of flesh with no shape or outline in it, then He begins shaping and shaping, and He forms from it a head, two hands, a chest, a belly, two thighs, two legs, and all the other organs, so sometimes the woman drops it before shaping and shaping, and sometimes she casts it after it has become a self Shape and layout, and for this reason the Almighty said: Then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, meaning as you see it, that We may make clear to you and We cause to remain in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, meaning sometimes it settles in the womb and the woman does not expel it or miscarry it, as Mujahid said in the Almighty’s statement: formed and unformed, he said: It is the miscarriage, created and uncreated. Then when forty days have passed while it is a lump of flesh, the Almighty sends an angel to it and he breathes the spirit into it and shapes it as God Almighty wills, of good and bad, male and female, and writes its provision and its life span, and whether it will be wretched or happy. It was also proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-A’mash on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he is the truthful and believed one, told us: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty nights, then he is a clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period, then God sends to him an angel who is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his deeds, his life span, and whether he will be wretched or happy, then the soul is breathed into him.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Dawud bin Abi Hind, from Al-Sha’bi, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: When the sperm settles in the womb, an angel takes it in his hand and says: O Lord, is it formed or unformed? If it is said: Unformed, then it was not a soul and the wombs expelled it as blood. If it is said: Formed, then he says: O Lord, male or female, wretched or doomed, what is the term and what is the effect, and in which land does it die? He said: Then it is said to the sperm: Who is your Lord? It says: God. Then it is said: Who provided for you? Then he says, God, and it is said to him, Go to the Mother of the Book, for you will find in it the story of this sperm. He said, It is created, lives its term, eats its sustenance, and treads its traces, until when its term comes, it dies and is buried in that place. Then Amer Al-Sha’bi recited, O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, some formed and some unformed. So when it reaches a lump of flesh, it is reversed in the fourth creation and becomes a soul. If it is unformed, the wombs expel it as blood. If it is formed, it is reversed in creation. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid, who reported it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The angel enters upon the sperm after it has settled in the womb for forty or forty-five days, and says: ‘O Lord, will I be wretched or will I be counted?’ God says, and they write, and he says: ‘A male or a female?’ God says, and they write, and he writes his deeds, his traces, his provision, and his life span. Then the scrolls are folded up and nothing is added to what is in them nor is anything subtracted from it.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah and from another chain of transmission from Abu al-Tayyib with a similar meaning. And His saying: Then We bring you forth as a child, meaning weak in body, hearing, sight, strength and mind, then God gives him strength little by little, and His parents are kind to him and have mercy on him during the hours of the night and the ends of the day. That is why He said: Then that you may reach your full strength, meaning that strength is complete and increases, and reaches the prime of youth and good appearance. And among you is he who is taken, meaning in the state of his youth and strength, And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, which is old age and decrepitude and weakness of strength, mind and understanding and the decline of states from senility and weakness of thought. That is why He said: So that he may not know anything after knowledge, as God Almighty said: “God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.” Al-Hafiz Abu Ya`la bin Ali bin Al-Muthanna Al-Mawsili said in his Musnad: Mansur bin Abi Muzahim told us, Khalid Al-Zayat told us, Dawud Abu Sulayman told me on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Muammar bin Hazm Al-Ansari on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The newborn, until he reaches puberty, whatever good deeds he does are recorded for his father or mother, and whatever bad deeds he does are not recorded against him or his parents. When he reaches puberty, God makes the pen run over him and orders the two angels who are with him to preserve and strengthen it. When he reaches forty years in Islam, God will protect him from the three afflictions: madness, leprosy, and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, God will lighten his account. When he reaches sixty, God will grant him the ability to repent to Him in a way that He loves. When he reaches seventy, the people of heaven will love him. When he reaches eighty, God will record his good deeds and overlook his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, God will forgive him his past and future sins, and will intercede for his family. He will be recorded as the trustee of God and he will be the prisoner of God on His earth. When he reaches the lowest age, so that he will not know after having known…” Something that God wrote down as much as he did in his health of good, but if he did evil, it was not written down against him.” This is a very strange hadith, and it is very objectionable. However, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated it in his Musnad with both a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: Abu al-Nadr told us, al-Faraj told us, Muhammad ibn ‘Aamir told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn ‘Abd God al-‘Aamri, on the authority of ‘Amr ibn Ha’far, on the authority of Anas, who said: “When a Muslim man reaches the age of forty, God will protect him from all kinds of calamities: madness, leprosy, and elephantiasis. When he reaches the age of fifty, God will make his reckoning easy. When he reaches the age of sixty, God will grant him repentance for which God will love him. When he reaches the age of seventy, God will love him and the people of the heavens will love him. When he reaches the age of eighty, God will accept his good deeds and erase his bad deeds. When he reaches the age of ninety, God will forgive him his past and future sins, and he will be called the prisoner of God on His earth and will intercede for his family.” Then he said: Hashim told us, al-Faraj told us, Muhammad ibn ‘Abd God al-‘Aamri told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn ‘Abd God ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman, on the authority of ‘Abd God ibn ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), similarly. Imam Ahmad also narrated: Anas bin Ayyad told us, Yusuf bin Abi Burdah Al-Ansari told me, on the authority of Ja’far bin Amr bin Umayyah Ad-Damri, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no long-lived person who lives forty years in Islam except that God will avert from him three types of affliction: insanity, leprosy, and elephantiasis.” He mentioned the rest of the hadith as it was mentioned above. It was narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shabib, on the authority of Abu Shaiba, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Malik, on the authority of Abu Qatada Al-Adawi, on the authority of my nephew Al-Zuhri, on the authority of his uncle, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no servant who lives forty years in Islam except that God will avert from him types of affliction: insanity, leprosy, and elephantiasis. So when he reaches fifty years of age, God will make his reckoning easy for him. So when he reaches sixty years of age, God will grant him the ability to repent to Him in a way that He loves. So when he reaches seventy years of age, God will forgive him his past and future sins, and he will be called the prisoner of God and the people of heaven will love him. So when he reaches At the age of eighty, God accepts his good deeds and overlooks his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, God forgives his past and future sins, and he is called God’s prisoner on His earth and intercedes for his family. His statement: “And you will see the earth lifeless” is another proof of His Almighty power to revive the dead, just as He revives the dead and lifeless earth, which is the barren land in which nothing grows. Qatada said: Dusty and crumbled. Al-Suddi said: Dead. Then when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [abundantly] of every beautiful pair meaning, when God sends down rain upon it, it quivers, i.e. moves with plants, and comes to life after its death, and swells, i.e. rises when the soil settles in it, then it grows what is in it of colors and kinds of fruits, crops, and various types of plants in different colors, tastes, smells, shapes, and benefits. For this reason, God the Almighty said: and grows [abundantly] of every beautiful pair meaning beautiful to look at and pleasant to smell. And His saying: That is because God is the Truth meaning the Creator, the Administrator, the Doer of whatever He wills and that He gives life to the dead meaning just as He gave life to the dead earth and caused these species to grow from it “Indeed, He who gives life to it is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent” His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is “And that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it” meaning it will happen, there is no doubt about it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves meaning He will return them after they have become dust in their graves and He will bring them into existence after they had ceased to exist, as God Almighty said: “And he has set forth for Us an example and has forgotten his own creation. He says, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’ Say, ‘He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation. Who made for you fire from the green tree, and then, behold, you kindle from it.” And there are many verses on this subject. Imam Ahmad said: Buhaiz narrated to us, Hammad bin Salamah narrated to us, he said: Ya`la bin Ata` informed us, on the authority of Wakee` bin Hadas, on the authority of his paternal uncle Abu Razeen Al-`Uqayli, whose name was Laqeet bin `Aamer, that he said: O Messenger of God, will all of us see our Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, on the Day of Resurrection, and what is the sign of that in His creation? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not all of you look at the moon alone? We said: Yes. He said: Then God is greater. He said: I said: O Messenger of God, how does God bring the dead back to life, and what is the sign of that in His creation? He said: Have you not passed by the valley of your people while they were still? He said: Yes. He said: Then did you pass by it while it was shaking with greenery? He said: Yes. He said: This is how God brings the dead back to life, and that is His sign in His creation. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah. Then Imam Ahmad also narrated it: Ali bin Ishaq told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Jaber told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, on the authority of Abu Razin Al-Uqayli, who said: “I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, how does God bring the dead back to life? He said: Did you pass by a barren land of your people, then pass by a fertile land? He said: Yes. He said: So is the resurrection.” And God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abis bin Marhum told us, Bakir bin Al-Sumait told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal, who said: Whoever knows that God is the manifest truth, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will resurrect those in the graves, will enter Paradise.

So when he reaches seventy years of age, God will forgive him his past and future sins, and he will be called the prisoner of God and the people of heaven will love him. So when he reaches At the age of eighty, God accepts his good deeds and overlooks his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, God forgives his past and future sins, and he is called God’s prisoner on His earth and intercedes for his family. His statement: “And you will see the earth lifeless” is another proof of His Almighty power to revive the dead, just as He revives the dead and lifeless earth, which is the barren land in which nothing grows. Qatada said: Dusty and crumbled. Al-Suddi said: Dead. Then when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows [abundantly] of every beautiful pair meaning, when God sends down rain upon it, it quivers, i.e. moves with plants, and comes to life after its death, and swells, i.e. rises when the soil settles in it, then it grows what is in it of colors and kinds of fruits, crops, and various types of plants in different colors, tastes, smells, shapes, and benefits. When he reaches puberty, God makes the pen run over him and orders the two angels who are with him to preserve and strengthen it. When he reaches forty years in Islam, God will protect him from the three afflictions: madness, leprosy, and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, God will lighten his account. When he reaches sixty, God will grant him the ability to repent to Him in a way that He loves. When he reaches seventy, the people of heaven will love him. When he reaches eighty, God will record his good deeds and overlook his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, God will forgive him his past and future sins, and will intercede for his family. He will be recorded as the trustee of God and he will be the prisoner of God on His earth. When he reaches the lowest age, so that he will not know after having known…” Something that God wrote down as much as he did in his health of good, but if he did evil, it was not written down against him.” This is a very strange hadith, and it is very objectionable. 22:8: When God Almighty mentioned the state of the ignorant, imitative misguidance in His statement: And among mankind is he who disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil, He mentioned in this the state of the callers to misguidance from the leaders of disbelief and innovations, saying: And among mankind is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book, meaning without sound reason or sound, explicit transmission, but rather with mere opinion and whims. And his saying: The second of his curves Ibn Abbas and others said: He is arrogant about the truth if he is called to it. Mujahid, Qatadah and Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam The second of his curves means he turns his neck, meaning he turns away from what he is called to of the truth, and he bends his neck in arrogance, like the saying of God the Almighty: And in Moses, when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority, but he turned away with his support (al-An’am 2:17). And God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger,’ you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion (al-An’am 2:17). And God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant (al-An’am 2:17). And Luqman said to his son, And do not turn your cheek away from people (al-An’am 2:17) meaning turn it away from them in arrogance towards them. And God the Almighty said: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away in arrogance (al-An’am 2:17). And His saying: To lead astray from the path of God. Some of them said: This is the lam of consequence, because He may not have intended that, and it is possible that it is the lam of justification. Then either what is meant by it are the obstinate ones, or what is meant by it is that this doer of this is We created him with this vile character in order to make him one of those who lead astray from the path of God. Then God the Almighty said: For him in this world is disgrace, which is humiliation and degradation, just as when he was arrogant about the signs of God, God met him with humiliation in this world and punished him in it before the Hereafter, because it was his greatest concern and the extent of his knowledge. “And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire. That is for what your hands have put forth,” meaning this will be said to him as a rebuke and a rebuke. And that God is not unjust to His servants, like His saying the Almighty: “Seize him and drag him to the level of Hellfire. Then pour over his head from the punishment of scalding water. Taste. Indeed, you are the Exalted in Might, the Generous. Indeed, this is what you were in doubt about.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad bin Al-Sabah told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hisham told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: It has reached me that one of them is burned seventy thousand times a day.

If he found what he liked, he would settle down, otherwise he would roll up his sleeves. Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim bin Al-Harith told us, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And among the people is he who worships God on the verge, he said: A man would come to Madinah, and if his wife gave birth to a boy and his horses produced a child, he would say: This is a good religion. But if his wife did not give birth and his horses did not produce a child, he would say: This is a bad religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq Al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Some of the Bedouins would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and convert to Islam. When they returned to their country, if they found a year of rain, a year of abundance, or a year of good births, they would say: This religion of ours is good, so hold fast to it. But if they found a year of drought, a year of bad births, or a year of famine, they would say: There is no good in this religion of ours. So God revealed to His Prophet, And among the people is he who worships God on the verge, If something good happens to him, he will be reassured by it. The verse. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When one of them came to Madinah, which was a land and environment, and his body was healthy there and his mare produced a good foal and his wife gave birth to a boy, he would be pleased with him and feel secure with him, and would say: I have not experienced anything but good since I have been on this religion of mine. But if a trial befalls him, and trial is an affliction, meaning if the pain of Madinah befalls him and his wife gives birth to a girl and the charity is delayed, Satan will come to him and say: By God, I have not experienced anything but evil since I have been on this religion of yours, and that is the trial. This is what Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Jurayj and more than one of the early Muslims mentioned in their interpretation of this verse. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: He is the hypocrite. If his worldly affairs are good for him, he continues to worship, but if his worldly affairs are corrupted and changed, he turns back and does not continue to worship except for what is good in his worldly affairs. If a trial, hardship, test or difficulty befalls him, he abandons his religion and returns to disbelief. Mujahid said about his statement: turns back on his face meaning he apostatizes as a disbeliever. His statement: He has lost this world and the Hereafter means that he has not gained anything from this world, and as for the Hereafter, he has disbelieved in God the Almighty, so he will be in the utmost misery and humiliation therein. For this reason, God the Almighty said: That is the manifest loss meaning this is the great loss and the losing deal. His statement: He calls upon, besides God, that which can neither harm him nor benefit him meaning of idols and rivals, he seeks their aid, support and provision, but they neither benefit him nor harm him. That is the farthest error. His statement: He calls upon one whose harm is nearer to him than his benefit meaning that his harm in this world before the Hereafter is nearer to his benefit in it. As for the Hereafter, his harm is certain and confirmed. And his saying: What an evil protector and what an evil companion. Mujahid said: It means the idol, meaning what an evil one is whom he called upon besides God as a protector, meaning a guardian and a helper, and what an evil companion, meaning the one who mixes and associates. Ibn Jarir chose that what is meant is what an evil cousin and companion is whoever worships God on the edge, if good befalls him he is content with it, but if a trial befalls him he turns back on his face. Mujahid’s saying that what is meant by it is the idol is more appropriate and closer to the context of the speech, and God knows best.
22:12: Mujahid, Qatada, and others said: On the edge is in doubt. Others said: On the edge, and from it comes the edge of the mountain, meaning its edge. That is, he entered the religion on an edge. If he found what he liked, he would settle down, otherwise he would roll up his sleeves. Al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim bin Al-Harith told us, Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And among the people is he who worships God on the verge, he said: A man would come to Madinah, and if his wife gave birth to a boy and his horses produced a child, he would say: This is a good religion. But if his wife did not give birth and his horses did not produce a child, he would say: This is a bad religion. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Ahmad bin Abdul Rahman told us, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Ishaq Al-Qummi, on the authority of Ja’far bin Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Some of the Bedouins would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and convert to Islam. When they returned to their country, if they found a year of rain, a year of abundance, or a year of good births, they would say: This religion of ours is good, so hold fast to it. But if they found a year of drought, a year of bad births, or a year of famine, they would say: There is no good in this religion of ours. 22:14: When He mentioned the wretched people of misguidance, He followed up by mentioning the happy righteous ones who believed in their hearts and confirmed their faith with their actions, so they did good deeds of all kinds of acts of worship, and abandoned evil deeds, which caused them to dwell in the high ranks in the gardens of Paradise. And when the Most High mentioned that He led those astray and guided these, He said: Indeed, God does what He wills.
22:15: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the sky, meaning the sky of his house, then let him cut it off, meaning let him strangle himself with it. This is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata’, Abu al-Jawza’, Qatadah and others said. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Let him extend a rope to the sky, meaning let him reach the sky, because victory only comes to Muhammad from the sky, then let him cut it off if he is able to do so. The statement of Ibn Abbas and his companions is more appropriate and clearer in meaning and more eloquent in sarcasm, because the meaning is: Whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad, his book and his religion, let him go and kill himself if that angers him, because God will inevitably support him. God the Most High said: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. This is why He said: So let him see whether his plan will remove that which enrages him. Al-Suddi said: He means that it is the affair of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him. Ata al-Khurasani said: Let him see if that will cure what he finds in his chest of anger. And His statement: And thus We have sent it down meaning the Qur’an as clear verses meaning clear in its wording and meaning, as an argument from God against the people, and that God guides whom He wills meaning He misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills, and He has the perfect wisdom and the decisive argument in that He is not questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned as for Him, it is due to His wisdom, mercy, justice, knowledge, power, and greatness that there is no objection to His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning.

22:17: God Almighty tells us about the people of these different religions, the believers and those other than them, the Jews and the Sabians. We have already presented in Surat Al-Baqarah the definition of them and the differences between people regarding them, the Christians and the Magians and those who associated partners with God and worshipped other than Him. God Almighty: will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection and will judge between them with justice. He will admit those who believe in Him into Paradise and those who disbelieve in Him into Hell. God Almighty is a witness over their actions, a guardian of their words, and a knower of their secrets and what their hearts conceal.
22:18: The Almighty informs us that He alone is worthy of worship, with no partner for Him. Everything prostrates to His greatness willingly or unwillingly, and the prostration of everything is specific to Him, as the Almighty said: Have they not seen what God has created of things, whose shadows turn to the right and the left, prostrating to God, while they are humbled? And He said here: Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth? That is, from the angels in the regions of the heavens, and the animals in all directions from mankind, jinn, beasts, and birds. And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. And His statement: And the sun, the moon, and the stars He only mentioned these explicitly, because they were worshipped instead of God, so He explained that they prostrate to their Creator and that they are created and subjugated. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to God, who created them verse. And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you know where this sun goes? I said: God. And His Messenger knows best. He said: “Then it goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then it is asked for permission, and soon it will be said to it: ‘Go back from whence you came.’” In Al-Musnad, Sunan Abi Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah in the hadith of the eclipse: The sun and the moon are two creations of God, and they do not eclipse for the death or life of anyone, but when God Almighty reveals Himself to one of His creation, it humbles itself before it. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: There is no star, sun or moon in the sky but that it prostrates to God when it sets, then it does not turn away until it is given permission to do so, so it takes the right side until it returns to its place of rising. As for the mountains and trees, their prostration is in the shade of their shadows to the right and left. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A man came and said: O Messenger of God, I saw myself last night while I was sleeping as if I was praying behind a tree, so I prostrated, and the tree prostrated to my prostration, and I heard it saying: O God, write for me with it a reward with You, remove from me a burden with it, and make it a store for me with You, and accept it from me as You accepted it from Your servant David. Ibn Abbas said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Prostration, then prostrated, and I heard him saying the same as the man told him about the tree’s saying.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih. And his saying: And the beasts means all animals. It was reported in the hadith from Imam Ahmad that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade taking the backs of beasts as pulpits. There is a mount that is better and remembers God more than its rider. And his saying: And many of the people means those who prostrate to God willingly and by choice, worshipping Him. And many upon whom the punishment is due means those who refuse, refuse, and are arrogant. “And he whom God humiliates will have no one to honor him. Indeed, God does what He wills.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Shaiban al-Ramli told us, al-Qaddah told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, who said: It was said to Ali: There is a man here who speaks about the will, so Ali said to him: O servant of God, did God create you as He wills or as you will? He said: Rather, as He wills. He said: So He makes you sick when He wills or when you will? He said: Rather, when He wills. He said: So He heals you when He wills or when you will? He said: Rather, when He wills. He said: So He admits you where you will or where He wills? He said: Rather, where He wills. He said: By God, if you had said anything else, I would have struck the one in your eyes with the sword. On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the son of Adam recites a verse of prostration, Satan withdraws weeping, saying: ‘Woe to me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate, and he prostrated, so Paradise is for him. I was commanded to prostrate, but I refused, so Hell is for me.’” Narrated by Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Sa’id, the freed slave of Banu Hashim, and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri’ told us: Ibn Lahi’ah told us: Mishrah ibn Ha’an Abu Mus’ab al-Ma’afiri told us: I heard Uqbah ibn Amir say: “I said: O Messenger of God, is Surah al-Hajj superior to the rest of the Qur’an because of its two prostrations?” He said: Yes, so whoever does not prostrate during them should not recite them. Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is not strong, and there is some doubt about this, because Ibn Lahi’ah explicitly stated that he heard it, and most of what they criticized him for was his concealment of the meaning. Abu Dawud said in Al-Marasil: Ahmad bin Amr bin Al-Sarh told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Amer bin Jashab, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, may God have mercy on him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Surat Al-Hajj is superior to the rest of the Qur’an by two prostrations. Then Abu Dawud said: This has been attributed, meaning from a different source, and it is not authentic. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Ismaili said: Ibn Abi Dawud told me, Yazid bin Abdullah told us, Al-Walid told us, Abu Amr told us, Hafs bin Annan told us, Nafi’ told me, he said: Abu Al-Jahm told me that Umar prostrated twice during Hajj while he was in Jabiyah, and he said: This is superior by two prostrations. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Al-Harith bin Saeed Al-Atqi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Manin, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Aas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to him fifteen prostrations in the Qur’an, three of which are in Al-Mufassal and two prostrations in Surat Al-Hajj. These are corroborating evidences that support each other.
22:19: It is proven in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qais bin Ibad on the authority of Abu Dharr: that he used to swear that this verse, These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord, was revealed about Hamza and his two companions, and Utbah and his two companions on the day they went out in Badr. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari when explaining it. Then Al-Bukhari said: Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, I heard my father, Abu Majlaz told us on the authority of Qais bin Ibad on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib that he said: I will be the first to kneel before the Most Merciful to dispute on the Day of Resurrection. Qais said: And about them was revealed: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord, he said: They are those who went out in battle on the day of Badr: Ali, Hamza, Ubaidah, Shaibah bin Rabi'ah, Utbah bin Rabi'ah, and Al-Walid bin Utbah. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it. Saeed bin Abi Aruba said on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: These are two opponents who have disputed about their Lord, he said: The Muslims and the People of the Book disputed, and the People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, so we are more deserving of God than you. The Muslims said: Our Book rules over all the books and our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, so we are more deserving of God than you. So God granted victory to Islam over those who opposed it, and revealed: These are two opponents who have disputed about their Lord. And Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And Shu’bah said on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: These are two opponents who have disputed about their Lord, he said: One who believes and one who denies. And Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid regarding this verse: Like the disbeliever and the believer who disputed about the resurrection, and he and Ata’ said in the narration of this verse: They are the believers and the disbelievers. And Ikrimah said: These are two opponents who disputed about their Lord. He said: They are Paradise and Hell. Hell said: Make me for punishment, and Paradise said: Make me for mercy. The statement of Mujahid and Ata’: What is meant by these are the disbelievers and the believers includes all the statements, and the story of the Day of Badr and others is included in it, because the believers want to support the religion of God the Almighty, and the disbelievers want to extinguish the light of faith, abandon the truth and make falsehood appear. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, and it is good. That is why he said: So those who disbelieved, garments of fire will be cut out for them, meaning pieces of fire will be cut out for them. Saeed bin Jubair said: Of copper, which is the hottest thing when heated. Pouring water will be poured over their heads, melting thereby that which is in their bellies and their skins, meaning if boiling water is poured over their heads, which is extremely hot water. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is molten copper. It melted the fat and intestines in their stomachs. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and others. Likewise, their skins melt. Ibn Abbas and Saeed said: It fell off. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me, Ibrahim Abu Ishaq al-Talaqani told me, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu al-Samh, on the authority of Ibn Hijrah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The boiling water will be poured over their heads and will penetrate their skulls until it reaches their stomachs, and what is in their stomachs will melt away until it reaches their feet. It is melting, then it will be returned to how it was.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak and said: Hasan Sahih. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in this way from his father, on the authority of Abu Na’im, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak with it. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Ahmad ibn Abi al-Hawari told us. He said: I heard Abdullah bin Al-Sarri say: The angel comes to him carrying a vessel with two dogs because of its heat, and when he brings it close to his face, he hates it. He said: Then he raises a whip with him and strikes his head with it, emptying his brain, then he empties the vessel of his brain and it reaches his stomach from his brain, and that is what he said: With it he melts what is in their bellies and their skins. And his saying: And for them are maces of iron. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a mace of iron were placed on the earth and the two heavy things were to come together for it, they would not lift it from the earth. Imam Ahmad said: Musa bin Dawud told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a mountain were struck with a mace of iron, it would shatter and then return to what it was. And if a bucket of filth were poured into the world, the people of the world would stink.” Ibn Abbas said about his saying: And for them are maces of iron, he said: They are struck with them, and every limb falls on its own and they call for destruction. And His statement: Whenever they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Abu Thabyan, on the authority of Salman, who said: The Fire is black and dark, and its flames and embers do not give light. Then he recited: Whenever they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it. Zayd ibn Aslam said about this verse: Whenever they want to get out of it, out of distress, they are returned to it. He said: It has reached me that the people of Hell will not breathe in Hell. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: By God, they do not hope to get out, for their feet are bound and their hands are shackled, but its flames will raise them and its whips will return them. And His statement: And taste the punishment of the burning fire is like His statement: And it will be said to them, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ The meaning of the statement is that they will be humiliated by the punishment in word and deed.

22:23: When God the Almighty informed about the state of the people of Hell - may God protect us from their state and what they are in of torment, punishment, burning, shackles, and what has been prepared for them of garments of fire - He mentioned the state of the people of Paradise. We ask God from His grace and generosity to admit them into Paradise. He said: "Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow" meaning they are penetrated in their environs, corners, and sides and under their trees and palaces, and they spend them as they wish and wherever they want. "They will be adorned therein with adornments of bracelets of gold and pearls" meaning on their hands, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the agreed upon hadith: "The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches." Ka'b al-Ahbar said: There is an angel in Paradise, if I wanted to name him, I would have named him. He has been making adornments for the people of Paradise since God created him until the Day of Resurrection. If he were to bring out a heart from it - meaning a bracelet from it - it would repel the rays of the sun as the sun repels the light of the moon. And his saying: And their garments therein will be silk is in contrast to the garments of the people of Hell that have been made for them. The garments of these people will be of silk, brocade and fine silk, as He said: “Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink. Indeed, this is your reward, and your effort is ever appreciated.” And in the Sahih: Do not wear silk or brocade in this world, for whoever wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter. Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: Whoever does not wear silk in the Hereafter will not enter Paradise. God Almighty said: And their garments therein will be silk. And His statement: And they are guided to the good of speech is like the statement of the Most High: “And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be admitted to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally by permission of their Lord. Their greeting therein will be, “Peace.” And His statement: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.” And His statement: “They will hear therein no ill speech or sin, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace.’” So they were guided to the place where they will hear good speech. And His statement: “And they will be met therein with greetings and peace.” Not like the people of the Fire will be humiliated by the words with which they are rebuked and rebuked, and it will be said to them: Taste the punishment of the burning fire. His statement: And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy means to the place where they praise their Lord for what He has done to them and bestowed upon them and bestowed upon them, as came in the authentic hadith: They are inspired to glorify and praise Him just as they are inspired to breathe. Some of the commentators said about His statement: And they are guided to the good of speech meaning the Qur’an, and it was said: There is no god but God, and it was said: the prescribed remembrances, And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy meaning the straight path in this world, and all of this does not contradict what we have mentioned, and God knows best.
