22:25: God the Almighty says, denouncing the infidels for preventing the believers from coming to the Sacred Mosque and performing their rituals therein and their claim that they are its guardians, "But they were not its guardians. Its guardians are only the righteous" Al-Baqarah 2:17. This verse is evidence that it was revealed in Madinah, as He said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:"They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Say, 'Fighting in it is a great sin. But averting people from the way of God and disbelief in Him and in Al-Masjid Al-Haram and expelling its people from it are greater in the sight of God.'" Al-Baqarah 2:17. And He said here: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert people from the way of God and Al-Masjid Al-Haram Al-Masjid Al-Haram meaning, among their characteristics is that, along with their disbelief, they avert people from the way of God and Al-Masjid Al-Haram, meaning, they avert from Al-Masjid Al-Haram whoever wants to go there from the believers who are the most deserving of it in reality. This construction in this verse is like the Almighty's statement: "Those who believe and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured." Al-Baqarah 2:17. And among their characteristics is that their hearts are assured by the remembrance of God. And His statement: Which We have made for mankind equal, whether he is staying there or traveling by, meaning they prevent people from reaching the Sacred Mosque, and God has made it an equal law, with no difference between the one residing therein and the one who is far away from it, equal for the one staying there or traveling by by, and from that is the equality of people in the quarters of Mecca and their residence, as Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas in His statement: equal for the one staying there or traveling by by, he said: The people of Mecca and others reside in the Sacred Mosque. Mujahid said: It is the same for the resident therein and the visitor therein. The people of Mecca and others are equal in their homes. This is what Abu Salih, Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah: It is the same for its people and others. This is the issue on which al-Shafi’i and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh differed in the mosque of al-Khayf, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal was also present. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, held that the quarters of Mecca are owned, inherited, and rented. He provided evidence with the hadith of al-Zuhri on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn on the authority of Amr ibn Uthman on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, will you stay in your house in Mecca tomorrow? He said: Did Aqeel leave us any quarters? Then he said: The infidel does not inherit from the Muslim, nor does the Muslim inherit from the infidel. This hadith is included in the two Sahihs, and it is proven that Umar ibn al-Khattab bought a house in Mecca from Safwan ibn Umayya and made it a prison, for four thousand dirhams. Tawus and Amr ibn Dinar said the same. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh held that it is not inherited or rented, which is the view of a group of the Salaf, and Mujahid and Ata’ stated it explicitly. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh cited as evidence what Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus on the authority of Umar ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Husayn, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Alqamah ibn Nadlah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr and Umar passed away, and the quarters of Mecca are not claimed except for the wandering ones. Whoever needs housing, he lives, and whoever is independent, he lives. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Ibn Mujahid on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that he said: It is not permissible to sell or rent the houses of Mecca. He also said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Ata’ used to forbid renting in the Haram, and he informed me that Umar bin Al-Khattab used to forbid the houses of Mecca to be divided so that the pilgrims would stay in their courtyards. The first one to divide his house was Suhayl bin Amr, so Umar bin Al-Khattab sent to him about that, and he said: Give me time, O Commander of the Faithful, for I was a merchant, and I wanted to make two doors that would hold my back. He said: Then you may do that. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid that Umar ibn al-Khattab said: O people of Mecca, do not make doors for your homes so that the nomad can stay wherever he wants. He said: Muammar informed us on the authority of someone who heard Ata’ say: The one who stays there and the nomad are the same. He said: They can stay wherever they want. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, with a chain of transmission ending with him: Whoever consumes the rent of the houses of Mecca will consume fire. Imam Ahmad took the middle position and said: It is owned and inherited, but not rented, combining the evidence. And God knows best. And his statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice or wrongdoing, We will make him taste a painful punishment. Some of the commentators among the people of Arabic said: The baa here is redundant, like his statement: It grows with oil, meaning it produces oil. And likewise his statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, meaning it causes an act of injustice, and as al-A’sha said. Our spears between the cauldrons and the bare frankness have guaranteed the livelihood of our children. The other said: In a Yemeni valley, the Shath grows at its top and bottom with Marakh and Shabhan. The best thing is that the verb here includes the meaning of to intend, and that is why he made it transitive with the preposition with, and said: And whoever intends therein to commit an abomination, meaning he intends therein to commit a terrible act of major sin. And his saying: with injustice, meaning intentionally, intending that it is injustice, not an interpretation, as Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, it is intention. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: By oppression of your polytheism. Mujahid said: That someone other than God is worshipped therein. Qatada and others said the same. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “By oppression is that you consider permissible in the Sacred Sanctuary what God has forbidden you, such as harm or killing, so you oppress those who would not oppress you and kill those who would not kill you. If you do that, then a painful punishment is due to you.” Mujahid said: By oppression, you do evil in it. This is a special feature of the Sacred Sanctuary, in that the one who begins evil in it is punished if he intends to do it, even if he does not commit it, as Ibn Abi Hatim said in his interpretation. Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Al-Suddi that he heard Abdullah narrating on one occasion, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, regarding His statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice, he said: If a man intends therein to commit an act of injustice while he is in Aden, God will make him taste a painful punishment. Shu’bah said: He raised it for us, but I will not raise it for you. Yazid said: He raised it, and Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Yazid bin Harun. I said: This chain of transmission is authentic according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari, and stopping it is more likely than raising it, and for this reason Shu’bah insisted on stopping it from the words of Ibn Mas’ud. Likewise, Asbat and Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, stopping it, and God knows best. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: There is no man who intends to commit a sin and it is recorded against him, even if a man in Aden Aban intended to kill a man in this house, God would make him taste a painful torment. Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said the same. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: It is a sin in it, no, by God, and yes, by God. And it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, something similar. Saeed bin Jubair said: Cursing a servant is injustice and what is greater. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Abdullah bin Ata’, on the authority of Maymun bin Mihran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And whoever intends therein an injustice or wrongdoing, he said: The ruler’s trade in it. On the authority of Ibn Omar: Selling food in Mecca is heresy. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: And whoever commits injustice and blasphemy therein, he said: The monopolist in Mecca, and more than one person said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Ishaq al-Jawhari told us, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Ja`far bin Yahya, on the authority of his uncle `Ammarah bin Thauban, Musa bin Bazan told me, on the authority of Ya`la bin Umayyah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hoarding food in Mecca is an abomination. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur`ah told us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Bakir told us, Ibn Lahi`ah told us, `Ata bin Dinar told us, Sa`id bin Jubayr told me: Ibn Abbas said regarding God’s statement: And whoever intends therein to commit an abomination or wrongdoing, he said: It was revealed about `Abdullah bin Unays, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him with two men: one of them was an emigrant and the other was from the Ansar. They boasted about their lineage, so `Abdullah bin Unays became angry and killed the Ansar, then he apostatized from Islam and fled to Mecca, so `And whoever intends therein to commit an abomination or wrongdoing,’ was revealed about him, meaning whoever takes refuge in the Haram with an abomination, meaning by turning away from… Islam, and these traces, although they indicate that these things are from atheism, it is more general than that, and in it there is a warning of what is more serious than that, and for this reason when the people of the elephant were about to destroy the House, God sent upon them birds in Ababil, pelting them with stones of baked clay * And made them like eaten straw, meaning he destroyed them and made them a lesson and a punishment for everyone who wanted to harm it, and for this reason it was established in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: An army will attack this House, and when they are in a desert on the earth, the first and the last of them will be swallowed up, the hadith. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Kanasa told us, Ishaq bin Saeed told us on the authority of his father, who said: Abdullah bin Omar came to Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr and said: O Ibn Al-Zubayr, beware of committing an act of blasphemy in the sanctuary of God, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A man from Quraysh will commit an act of blasphemy in it, and if his sins were weighed against the sins of the two worlds, they would outweigh them. So be careful not to be him. He also said in the Musnad of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas: Hashim told us, Ishaq bin Saeed told us, Saeed bin Amr told us: Abdullah bin Omar came to Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr while he was sitting in the Hijr and said: O Ibn Al-Zubayr, beware of committing an act of blasphemy in the sanctuary, for I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: He will undo it and a man from Quraysh will commit it, and if his sins were weighed against the sins of the two worlds, they would outweigh them. He said: Be careful not to be him. None of the authors of the books narrated it from these two sources.
22:26: This is a rebuke and rebuke to those Quraysh who worshipped other than God and associated partners with Him in the spot that was founded from the first day on the oneness of God and worshipping Him alone, with no partner for Him. So God Almighty mentioned that He assigned Abraham the location of the House, meaning He guided him to it and handed it over to him and permitted him to build it. Many of those who said that Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to build the Ancient House, and that it had not been built before him, used it as evidence, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Dharr, I said: “O Messenger of God, which mosque was established first? He said: The Sacred Mosque. I said: Then which? He said: The Holy House. I said: How many years are between them? He said: Forty years.” God the Almighty said: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed verses 20. He also said: “And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying, ‘Purify My House for those who go around it, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate. ’” We have already mentioned what was mentioned about the construction of the House in the Sahihs and Athars, so there is no need to repeat it here. God the Almighty said here: That you do not associate anything with Me, meaning a son in My name alone. And purify My House, Qatadah and Mujahid said: from polytheism. For those who go around it, and those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate, meaning make it purely for those who worship God alone, with no partner for Him. The one who goes around it is known, and it is the most specific act of worship at the House, as it is not done in any other spot on earth. And those who stand, meaning in prayer. That is why He said: And those who bow and prostrate, so He linked circumambulation with prayer because they are not prescribed except specifically for the House. Circumambulation at it and prayer towards it are in most cases, except for what is exempted from prayer when the direction of the qibla is unclear, in war, and in voluntary prayer while traveling. God knows best. And His statement: And proclaim to the people the Hajj means call to the people to perform Hajj, inviting them to perform Hajj to this House which We have commanded you to build. It is mentioned that he said: O Lord, how can I convey it to the people when my voice will not reach them? He said: Call and we will convey it. So he stood in his place, and it was said on the Black Stone, and it was said on Safa, and it was said on Abu Qubays, and said: O people, your Lord has established a House, so perform Hajj to it. It is said that the mountains humbled themselves until the sound reached the corners of the earth, and those in the wombs and loins heard, and everything that heard it answered him from stone, mud, and trees, and whoever God had written to perform Hajj until the Day of Resurrection, Here I am, O God, here I am. This is the gist of what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, and more than one of the Salaf, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim included it in full. And His saying: They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel the verse, this verse may be used as evidence by some scholars who have said that Hajj on foot for those who are able to do it is better than Hajj on a horse, because He mentioned them first, which indicates the importance of them and the strength of their determination and resolve. Waki’ said on the authority of Abu Al-Umais, on the authority of Abu Halhalah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Nothing has wronged me except my brother. I wish that I had performed Hajj on foot, because God says: They will come to you on foot the verse, and what the majority are of is that Hajj on a horse is better, following the example of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he performed Hajj on a horse despite his complete strength, peace be upon him. His saying: They come from every pass means a path, as He said: And We made therein paths as roads. His saying: Deep means far, as stated by Mujahid, Ata’, As-Suddi, Qatadah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Ath-Thawri and more than one. This verse is like the saying of God Almighty, informing us about Abraham when he said in his supplication: So make hearts among the people yearn toward them. There is no one among the people of Islam who does not yearn to see the Kaaba and circumambulate it, as people come to it from all directions and regions.

22:28: Ibn Abbas said: That they may witness benefits for themselves. He said: The benefits of this world and the Hereafter. As for the benefits of the Hereafter, they are the pleasure of God, and as for the benefits of this world, they are what they obtain of bounty from the body, sacrifices, and trade. Mujahid and others said the same: They are the benefits of this world and the Hereafter, like His statement: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. And His statement: And mention the name of God on appointed days over what He has provided for them of livestock. Shu'bah and Hisham said on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa'id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The appointed days are the ten days. Al-Bukhari connected it to him with a definitive formula. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ata', Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Ata' al-Khurasani, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. This is the view of al-Shafi'i and the well-known view on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Arara narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There are no days in which good deeds are better than these. They said: Not even jihad in the cause of God? He said: Not even jihad in the cause of God, unless a man goes out risking his life and his wealth and does not return with anything. Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah in a similar manner. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is a good, strange, authentic hadith. There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, Abu Hurayrah, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr and Jabir. I said: I have investigated these chains of narration and devoted a separate section to them. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: ‘Uthman narrated to us, Abu ‘Awanah informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are no days greater before God, nor are deeds more beloved to Him in them than these ten days, so increase in them the tahlil, takbir and tahmid. It was narrated from another chain of narration on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Omar and Abu Hurairah would go out to the market during the ten days and say the takbir, and the people would say the takbir after them. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that these are the ten days by which He swore in His statement: By the dawn and ten nights. Some of the early Muslims said: This is what is meant by His statement: And We completed them with ten. In Sunan Abi Dawud, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast these ten days. These ten days include the Day of Arafah, which is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Qatadah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about fasting the Day of Arafah, and he said: I hope that God will expiate for the sins of the past and coming year by it. It also includes the Day of Sacrifice, which is the greatest day of Hajj.” It was narrated in a hadith that it is the best of days with God. In short, it has been said that these ten days are the best days of the year, as stated in the hadith, and it is much better than the last ten days of Ramadan, because what is prescribed in these days is prescribed in them, such as prayer, fasting, charity, and other things. This is distinguished by the fact that it is specifically for performing the obligation of Hajj. It was said that this is better because it includes the Night of Decree, which is better than a thousand months. Others took a middle course and said: The days of this are better, and the nights of that are better. This brings together the evidence, and God knows best. Second statement Regarding the specified days. Al-Hakam said on the authority of Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The specified days are the Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Ahmad Ibn Hanbal agreed with it in a narration on his authority. A third statement Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Ibn Ajlan told us, Nafi’ told me that Ibn Umar used to say: The known and numbered days are all four days. The known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the numbered days are three days after the Day of Sacrifice. This is a sound chain of transmission to him, and al-Suddi said it, and it is the school of thought of Imam Malik ibn Anas. This statement and the one before it are supported by the Almighty’s statement: For what He has provided for them of cattle, meaning the remembrance of God when slaughtering them. Fourth statement It is the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and another day after it, and this is the school of thought of Abu Hanifa. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told me on the authority of his father that he said: The known things are the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashreeq. And His statement: On what He has provided for them of the grazing livestock means camels, cows and sheep as God has detailed in Surat Al-An’am eight pairs the verse, and His statement: So eat from them and feed the poor and needy this verse was used as evidence by those who held that eating from the sacrificial animals is obligatory, and this is a strange statement, and what most people hold is that it is a matter of permission or recommendation, as “it has been proven that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) slaughtered his sacrifice, he ordered a piece of each sacrificial animal to be cooked, so he ate from its meat and drank from its broth.” Abdullah bin Wahb said: Malik said to me: I like him to eat from his sacrificial animal, because God says: So eat from it. Ibn Wahb said: I asked Al-Layth, and he said the same to me, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim: So eat from it. He said: The polytheists did not eat from their slaughtered animals, so permission was given to the Muslims, so whoever wanted to eat could eat and whoever did not want to could not eat, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’. Hisham said, on the authority of Hisn, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: Then eat from it, he said: It is like His statement: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt, “And when the prayer is concluded, then disperse within the land,” and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his interpretation. And he provided evidence from Nasr regarding the statement that half of the sacrificial animals should be given in charity, based on His statement in this verse: Then eat from it and feed the poor and needy, so he divided it into two halves: one half for the one making the sacrifice and one half for the poor. The other statement is that it should be divided into three parts: one third for him, one third for him to give as a gift, and one third for him to give in charity, based on the statement of God Almighty in the other verse: Then eat from it and feed the contented and the needy, and we will discuss it later, God willing, and He is trustworthy. And his saying: The wretched, the needy. Ikrimah said: He is the one who is forced and who appears to be miserable and the poor who is self-sufficient. Mujahid said: He is the one who does not extend his hand. Qatadah said: It is the time. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It is the blind. And his saying: Then let them complete their ceremonies. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is putting on the ihram of shaving the head, wearing clothes, cutting the nails and the like. And this is how Ata’ and Mujahid narrated on his authority, and this is what Ikrimah and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said. And Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then let them complete their ceremonies. He said: The ceremonies are the rituals. And his saying: And fulfill their vows. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It means slaughtering what he vowed of the sacrificial animals. And Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And fulfill their vows The vow of Hajj and the sacrificial animals and whatever a person vows of something that is during Hajj. Ibrahim bin Maysarah said on the authority of Mujahid, And fulfill their vows, he said: sacrifices. Laith bin Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid, And fulfill their vows, every vow for a specified period. Ikrimah said, And fulfill their vows, he said: their Hajj. And Imam Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated likewise: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us regarding his statement, And fulfill their vows, he said: the vows of Hajj. So everyone who enters Hajj must perform the acts of worship in it, such as circumambulating the House, between Safa and Marwa, Arafat and Muzdalifah, and throwing stones at the Jamarat as they were commanded. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Malik. And his saying: And let them go around the Ancient House. Mujahid said: He means the obligatory circumambulation on the Day of Sacrifice. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Abu Hamza who said: Ibn Abbas said to me: Do you recite Surat Al-Hajj, God Almighty says: And let them go around the Ancient House. The last of the rituals is circumambulating the Ancient House. I said: And this is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. When he returned to Mina on the Day of Sacrifice, he began by throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat, and he threw seven pebbles at it. Then he slaughtered his sacrificial animal and shaved his head. Then he performed the Ifadah and circumambulated the House. In the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The people were commanded that the last thing they should do around the House should be circumambulation, except that it was made easier for the menstruating woman. And his saying: By the Ancient House is evidence for those who say that it is obligatory to circumambulate from behind the Black Stone, because it is from the foundation of the House that Abraham built, even though the Quraysh had removed it from the House when they were short of money. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated from behind the Black Stone and informed that the Black Stone was from the House and did not touch the two Syrian corners because they were not completed on the ancient foundations of Abraham. For this reason, Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar Al-Adani told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Hisham bin Hajar on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed, And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated from behind it. Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding his saying: And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, he said: Because it was the first House established for the people. And Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said the same, and on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: The House was called the Ancient House because it was freed on the day of the flood in the time of Noah. And Khasif said: It was called the Ancient House because no tyrant ever prevailed over it. Ibn Abi Nujayh and Laith narrated from Mujahid: He was freed from the tyrants so that they would not have power over him. Qatada said the same. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Humayd from al-Hasan ibn Muslim from Mujahid: Because no one intended to harm him except that he perished. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Muammar from al-Zuhri from Ibn al-Zubayr who said: The Ancient House was called that because God freed it from the tyrants. Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Ismail and others narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth informed me from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid from Ibn Shihab from Muhammad ibn Urwah from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Ancient House was called that because no tyrant prevailed over it. Ibn Jarir narrated it the same way from Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Najjari from Abdullah ibn Salih with it, and he said: If it is authentic, Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and strange hadith, then he narrated it from another chain of transmission from al-Zuhri as a mursal.

There are narrations on this topic on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, Abu Hurayrah, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr and Jabir. I said: I have investigated these chains of narration and devoted a separate section to them. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: ‘Uthman narrated to us, Abu ‘Awanah informed us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are no days greater before God, nor are deeds more beloved to Him in them than these ten days, so increase in them the tahlil, takbir and tahmid. It was narrated from another chain of narration on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar in a similar manner. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Omar and Abu Hurairah would go out to the market during the ten days and say the takbir, and the people would say the takbir after them. Ahmad narrated on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that these are the ten days by which He swore in His statement: By the dawn and ten nights. Some of the early Muslims said: This is what is meant by His statement: And We completed them with ten. In Sunan Abi Dawud, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to fast these ten days. These ten days include the Day of Arafah, which is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Qatadah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about fasting the Day of Arafah, and he said: I hope that God will expiate for the sins of the past and coming year by it. It also includes the Day of Sacrifice, which is the greatest day of Hajj.” It was narrated in a hadith that it is the best of days with God. In short, it has been said that these ten days are the best days of the year, as stated in the hadith, and it is much better than the last ten days of Ramadan, because what is prescribed in these days is prescribed in them, such as prayer, fasting, charity, and other things. This is distinguished by the fact that it is specifically for performing the obligation of Hajj. It was said that this is better because it includes the Night of Decree, which is better than a thousand months. Others took a middle course and said: The days of this are better, and the nights of that are better. This brings together the evidence, and God knows best. Second statement Regarding the specified days. Al-Hakam said on the authority of Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The specified days are the Day of Sacrifice and the three days after it. This is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and Ahmad Ibn Hanbal agreed with it in a narration on his authority. A third statement Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali ibn al-Madini told us, Yahya ibn Saeed told us, Ibn Ajlan told us, Nafi’ told me that Ibn Umar used to say: The known and numbered days are all four days. The known days are the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, and the numbered days are three days after the Day of Sacrifice. This is a sound chain of transmission to him, and al-Suddi said it, and it is the school of thought of Imam Malik ibn Anas. This statement and the one before it are supported by the Almighty’s statement: For what He has provided for them of cattle, meaning the remembrance of God when slaughtering them. Fourth statement It is the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and another day after it, and this is the school of thought of Abu Hanifa. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam told me on the authority of his father that he said: The known things are the Day of Arafah, the Day of Sacrifice, and the Days of Tashreeq. And His statement: On what He has provided for them of the grazing livestock means camels, cows and sheep as God has detailed in Surat Al-An’am eight pairs the verse, and His statement: So eat from them and feed the poor and needy this verse was used as evidence by those who held that eating from the sacrificial animals is obligatory, and this is a strange statement, and what most people hold is that it is a matter of permission or recommendation, as “it has been proven that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) slaughtered his sacrifice, he ordered a piece of each sacrificial animal to be cooked, so he ate from its meat and drank from its broth.” Abdullah bin Wahb said: Malik said to me: I like him to eat from his sacrificial animal, because God says: So eat from it. Ibn Wahb said: I asked Al-Layth, and he said the same to me, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Ibrahim: So eat from it. He said: The polytheists did not eat from their slaughtered animals, so permission was given to the Muslims, so whoever wanted to eat could eat and whoever did not want to could not eat, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’. Hisham said, on the authority of Hisn, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: Then eat from it, he said: It is like His statement: And when you are in a state of ihram, then hunt, “And when the prayer is concluded, then disperse within the land,” and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his interpretation. And he provided evidence from Nasr regarding the statement that half of the sacrificial animals should be given in charity, based on His statement in this verse: Then eat from it and feed the poor and needy, so he divided it into two halves: one half for the one making the sacrifice and one half for the poor. The other statement is that it should be divided into three parts: one third for him, one third for him to give as a gift, and one third for him to give in charity, based on the statement of God Almighty in the other verse: Then eat from it and feed the contented and the needy, and we will discuss it later, God willing, and He is trustworthy. And his saying: The wretched, the needy. Ikrimah said: He is the one who is forced and who appears to be miserable and the poor who is self-sufficient. Mujahid said: He is the one who does not extend his hand. Qatadah said: It is the time. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It is the blind. And his saying: Then let them complete their ceremonies. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is putting on the ihram of shaving the head, wearing clothes, cutting the nails and the like. And this is how Ata’ and Mujahid narrated on his authority, and this is what Ikrimah and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said. And Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then let them complete their ceremonies. He said: The ceremonies are the rituals. And his saying: And fulfill their vows. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It means slaughtering what he vowed of the sacrificial animals. And Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: And fulfill their vows The vow of Hajj and the sacrificial animals and whatever a person vows of something that is during Hajj. Ibrahim bin Maysarah said on the authority of Mujahid, And fulfill their vows, he said: sacrifices. Laith bin Abi Salim said on the authority of Mujahid, And fulfill their vows, every vow for a specified period. Ikrimah said, And fulfill their vows, he said: their Hajj. And Imam Ahmad and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated likewise: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us regarding his statement, And fulfill their vows, he said: the vows of Hajj. So everyone who enters Hajj must perform the acts of worship in it, such as circumambulating the House, between Safa and Marwa, Arafat and Muzdalifah, and throwing stones at the Jamarat as they were commanded. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Malik. And his saying: And let them go around the Ancient House. Mujahid said: He means the obligatory circumambulation on the Day of Sacrifice. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad told us on the authority of Abu Hamza who said: Ibn Abbas said to me: Do you recite Surat Al-Hajj, God Almighty says: And let them go around the Ancient House. The last of the rituals is circumambulating the Ancient House. I said: And this is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. When he returned to Mina on the Day of Sacrifice, he began by throwing the pebbles at the Jamarat, and he threw seven pebbles at it. Then he slaughtered his sacrificial animal and shaved his head. Then he performed the Ifadah and circumambulated the House. In the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The people were commanded that the last thing they should do around the House should be circumambulation, except that it was made easier for the menstruating woman. And his saying: By the Ancient House is evidence for those who say that it is obligatory to circumambulate from behind the Black Stone, because it is from the foundation of the House that Abraham built, even though the Quraysh had removed it from the House when they were short of money. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated from behind the Black Stone and informed that the Black Stone was from the House and did not touch the two Syrian corners because they were not completed on the ancient foundations of Abraham. For this reason, Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Omar Al-Adani told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Hisham bin Hajar on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When this verse was revealed, And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated from behind it. Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri regarding his saying: And let them circumambulate the Ancient House, he said: Because it was the first House established for the people. And Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said the same, and on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: The House was called the Ancient House because it was freed on the day of the flood in the time of Noah. And Khasif said: It was called the Ancient House because no tyrant ever prevailed over it. Ibn Abi Nujayh and Laith narrated from Mujahid: He was freed from the tyrants so that they would not have power over him. Qatada said the same. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Humayd from al-Hasan ibn Muslim from Mujahid: Because no one intended to harm him except that he perished. Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Muammar from al-Zuhri from Ibn al-Zubayr who said: The Ancient House was called that because God freed it from the tyrants. Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Ismail and others narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth informed me from Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid from Ibn Shihab from Muhammad ibn Urwah from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Ancient House was called that because no tyrant prevailed over it. Ibn Jarir narrated it the same way from Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Najjari from Abdullah ibn Salih with it, and he said: If it is authentic, Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and strange hadith, then he narrated it from another chain of transmission from al-Zuhri as a mursal.
22:30: God Almighty says: This is what we have been commanded to do of acts of obedience in performing the rituals and the great reward for the one who does them. And whoever honors the sacred limits of God meaning whoever avoids His sins and prohibitions and committing them is great in his soul, it is better for him with his Lord meaning he will have much good and great reward for that. Just as there is great reward and great recompense for doing acts of obedience, so too there is great reward and great recompense for those prohibitions and avoiding the forbidden things. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said regarding His statement: “That is so. And whoever honors the sacred limits of God” he said: The sacred limits are Mecca, Hajj, Umrah, and all of the sins that God has forbidden. Ibn Zayd said the same. And His statement: And grazing livestock have been made lawful to you, except what is recited to you, meaning, We have made lawful to you all grazing livestock, and what God has made lawful of bahīrah, sa’ībah, wasīlah, and Ḥām. And His statement: Except what is recited to you, meaning, the prohibition of dead animals, blood, pork, and that which has been dedicated to other than God, and the strangled animal, and the verse. Ibn Jarir said that, and he narrated it from Qatadah. And His statement: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement, from here is to clarify the type, meaning, avoid the uncleanness which is idols. And polytheism with God is linked to false statement, like His statement: “Say, ‘My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin and oppression without right, and that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about God that which you do not know.’” And from this is false testimony. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Bakra, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins? We said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: Associating partners with God, disobeying parents. He was reclining, then he sat up and said: “Beware of false speech. Beware of false testimony.” He kept repeating it until we said: If only he would stop. Imam Ahmad said: Marwan bin Muawiyah Al-Fazari told us, Sufyan bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Fatik bin Fadalah, on the authority of Ayman bin Khuraim, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up as a preacher and said: O people, false testimony is equal to associating partners with God three times. Then he recited: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. And this is how Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Mani’ on the authority of Marwan bin Muawiyah, then he said: It is strange. We only know it from the hadith of Sufyan bin Ziyad, and there is disagreement about the narration of this hadith from him, and we do not know that Ayman bin Khuraim heard it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us, Sufyan Al-Asfari told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Habib bin Al-Nu’man Al-Asadi on the authority of Khuraim bin Fatik Al-Asadi, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer, and when he finished, he stood up and said: False testimony is equal to associating partners with God, the Almighty and Majestic.” Then he recited this verse: So avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false statement. Idols and avoid false statement, being upright for God, not associating anything with Him.” Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Asim ibn Abi al-Najud on the authority of Wa’il ibn Rabi’ah on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: False testimony is equal to associating anything with God. Then he recited this verse. And His statement: Hanifā’ being devoted to God means sincerely devoted to Him in religion, deviating from falsehood and intending to follow the truth. For this reason He said: not associating anything with Him. Then He gave an example of the polytheist in his misguidance, destruction, and distance from guidance, saying: And whoever associates anything with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky meaning he had fallen from it and the birds had snatched him meaning the birds had torn him apart in the air or the wind had thrown him into a remote place meaning far away and deadly to whoever fell into it. For this reason it came in the hadith of al-Barā’: When the angels of death take the soul of the disbeliever and they ascend with his soul to the heavens, the gates of heaven are not opened for him, but his soul is thrown out from there. Then He recited this verse. The hadith has already been presented in Surah Ibrahim with its letters, wording, and chains. And God the Almighty gave another example of the polytheists in Surah al-An’am. And His saying: “Say: Shall we call upon besides God that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and turn back on our heels after God has guided us, like one whom the devils have led astray in the land, bewildered? He has companions who invite him to guidance, ‘Come to us.’ Say: Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance.”

22:32: God Almighty says this: And whoever honors the symbols of God meaning His commands it is from the piety of the hearts and from that is honoring gifts and bodies, as Al-Hakam said on the authority of Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Honoring them means appreciating them and praising them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas “That is it. And whoever honors the symbols of God” he said: appreciating them, appreciating them, and praising them. Abu Umamah ibn Sahl said: We used to fatten the sacrificial animal in Madinah, and the Muslims used to fatten it. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The blood of a white animal is more beloved to God than the blood of two black animals. Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Majah. They said: The white animal is the one that is white, but not dazzlingly white. The white one is better than the other, and other animals are also sufficient, as is proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two horned white rams. And on the authority of Abu Saeed, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed a horned black ram that ate in black, looked in black, and walked in black.” Narrated by the people of Sunan and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi - meaning that it had a black spot in these places. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two large, fat, horned, white, and scaly rams.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated on the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two horned, white, and scaly rams. It was said: They are the eunuchs, and it was said: Those whose testicles he had crushed and not cut off.” And God knows best. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to examine the eye and ear, and not to sacrifice an animal with a horn that is opposite, or a back, or a squint, or a hole in its ear.” Narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan, and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi, and they have it on his authority. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or ear.” Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The broken horn is half or more. Some linguists said: If its upper horn is broken, then it is broken, but the broken lower one is the breaking of the lower one, and the cutting of the ear is cutting off part of it. According to Al-Shafi’i, the sacrifice is acceptable, but it is disliked. Ahmad said: The sacrifice is not acceptable if the horn or ear is cut off, because of this hadith. Malik said: If blood is flowing from the horn, it is not acceptable, otherwise it is acceptable. And God knows best. As for the muqabalah, it is the one whose ear has been cut off in front, and the mudabarah from the back of her ear, and the sharqa’ is the one whose ear has been cut off lengthwise, as Al-Shafi’i said. As for the kharaqa’, it is the one whose ear has been pierced by a circular mark, and God knows best. On the authority of Al-Bara’, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four things are not permissible in sacrifice: the one-eyed whose blindness is obvious, the sick whose sickness is obvious, the lame whose limp is obvious, and the broken one that cannot be removed.” Narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan, and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi. These defects reduce the meat due to their weakness and inability to complete grazing because the sheep precede them to the pasture. Therefore, sacrificing them is not permissible according to Al-Shafi’i and other imams, as is apparent in the hadith. Al-Shafi’i’s statement regarding the one that is slightly sick differed into two opinions. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Utbah bin Abd Al-Salami that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the yellowed, the uprooted, the blemished, the broken, and the emaciated. It was said that the yellowed is the one that is emaciated, and it was said that the one that has its ear removed, and the blemished is the one-eyed, and the blemished is the one that continues to follow the sheep and does not follow because of its weakness, and the broken is the lame. All of these defects prevent If a defect occurs after the sacrifice has been designated, then it does not matter according to Al-Shafi’i, contrary to Abu Hanifa. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id who said: I bought a ram to sacrifice, and a wolf attacked and took the tailbone, so I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Sacrifice it. That is why it was mentioned in the hadeeth that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered us to examine the eye and ear, meaning that the gift or sacrifice should be fat, good and valuable, as narrated by Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawood on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: Umar gave a gift of a purebred camel and was given three hundred dinars for it. So he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of God, I gave a purebred camel as a gift and was given three hundred dinars for it. Should I sell it and buy a sacrificial animal with its price?” He said: No, I will slaughter it. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the sacrificial animal is among the rites of God. Muhammad ibn Abi Musa said: Standing, Muzdalifah, the Jamarat, stoning, shaving the head and the sacrificial animal are among the rites of God. Ibn Umar said: The greatest of the rites is the Ka’ba. His statement: Therein you have benefits means you have benefits from the body, from its milk, wool, fur, hair, and riding it for a specified term. Muqsim said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Therein you have benefits for a specified term: He said: As long as it is not called a body. Mujahid said regarding his statement: Therein you have benefits for a specified term: He said: Riding, milk, and children. So if it is called a camel or a sacrificial animal, all of that is gone. This is what Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and others said. Others said: Rather, he may benefit from it, even if it is a sacrificial animal, if he needs to do so, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man leading a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it. He said: It is a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it, woe to you, the second or third time.” In a narration by Muslim on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Ride it in a reasonable manner if you are forced to ride it. Shu’bah said on the authority of Zuhair on the authority of Abu Thabit al-Ama on the authority of al-Mughirah on the authority of Ali that he saw a man leading a sacrificial animal with its offspring, so he said: Do not drink from its milk except what is left over from its offspring. Then when the day of sacrifice comes, slaughter it and its offspring. His statement: Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House means the place of the offering and its end at the Ancient House, which is the Kaaba, as God Almighty said: An offering reaching the Kaaba and He said: And the offering is bent so that it reaches its place. We have already discussed the meaning of the Ancient House a little while ago, and praise be to God. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ who said: Ibn Abbas used to say: Whoever circumambulates the House has become free from the obligation. God Almighty said: Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.

Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Majah. They said: The white animal is the one that is white, but not dazzlingly white. The white one is better than the other, and other animals are also sufficient, as is proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two horned white rams. And on the authority of Abu Saeed, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed a horned black ram that ate in black, looked in black, and walked in black.” Narrated by the people of Sunan and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi - meaning that it had a black spot in these places. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two large, fat, horned, white, and scaly rams.” Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated on the authority of Jabir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two horned, white, and scaly rams. It was said: They are the eunuchs, and it was said: Those whose testicles he had crushed and not cut off.” And God knows best. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to examine the eye and ear, and not to sacrifice an animal with a horn that is opposite, or a back, or a squint, or a hole in its ear.” Narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan, and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi, and they have it on his authority. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from sacrificing an animal with a broken horn or ear.” Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: The broken horn is half or more. Some linguists said: If its upper horn is broken, then it is broken, but the broken lower one is the breaking of the lower one, and the cutting of the ear is cutting off part of it. According to Al-Shafi’i, the sacrifice is acceptable, but it is disliked. Ahmad said: The sacrifice is not acceptable if the horn or ear is cut off, because of this hadith. Malik said: If blood is flowing from the horn, it is not acceptable, otherwise it is acceptable. And God knows best. As for the muqabalah, it is the one whose ear has been cut off in front, and the mudabarah from the back of her ear, and the sharqa’ is the one whose ear has been cut off lengthwise, as Al-Shafi’i said. As for the kharaqa’, it is the one whose ear has been pierced by a circular mark, and God knows best. On the authority of Al-Bara’, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four things are not permissible in sacrifice: the one-eyed whose blindness is obvious, the sick whose sickness is obvious, the lame whose limp is obvious, and the broken one that cannot be removed.” Narrated by Ahmad and the people of Sunan, and authenticated by Al-Tirmidhi. These defects reduce the meat due to their weakness and inability to complete grazing because the sheep precede them to the pasture. Therefore, sacrificing them is not permissible according to Al-Shafi’i and other imams, as is apparent in the hadith. Al-Shafi’i’s statement regarding the one that is slightly sick differed into two opinions. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Utbah bin Abd Al-Salami that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the yellowed, the uprooted, the blemished, the broken, and the emaciated. It was said that the yellowed is the one that is emaciated, and it was said that the one that has its ear removed, and the blemished is the one-eyed, and the blemished is the one that continues to follow the sheep and does not follow because of its weakness, and the broken is the lame. All of these defects prevent If a defect occurs after the sacrifice has been designated, then it does not matter according to Al-Shafi’i, contrary to Abu Hanifa. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id who said: I bought a ram to sacrifice, and a wolf attacked and took the tailbone, so I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: Sacrifice it. That is why it was mentioned in the hadeeth that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered us to examine the eye and ear, meaning that the gift or sacrifice should be fat, good and valuable, as narrated by Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawood on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar who said: Umar gave a gift of a purebred camel and was given three hundred dinars for it. So he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Messenger of God, I gave a purebred camel as a gift and was given three hundred dinars for it. Should I sell it and buy a sacrificial animal with its price?” He said: No, I will slaughter it. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the sacrificial animal is among the rites of God. Muhammad ibn Abi Musa said: Standing, Muzdalifah, the Jamarat, stoning, shaving the head and the sacrificial animal are among the rites of God. Ibn Umar said: The greatest of the rites is the Ka’ba. His statement: Therein you have benefits means you have benefits from the body, from its milk, wool, fur, hair, and riding it for a specified term. Muqsim said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Therein you have benefits for a specified term: He said: As long as it is not called a body. Mujahid said regarding his statement: Therein you have benefits for a specified term: He said: Riding, milk, and children. So if it is called a camel or a sacrificial animal, all of that is gone. This is what Ata’, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and others said. Others said: Rather, he may benefit from it, even if it is a sacrificial animal, if he needs to do so, as is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man leading a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it. He said: It is a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it, woe to you, the second or third time.” In a narration by Muslim on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Ride it in a reasonable manner if you are forced to ride it. Shu’bah said on the authority of Zuhair on the authority of Abu Thabit al-Ama on the authority of al-Mughirah on the authority of Ali that he saw a man leading a sacrificial animal with its offspring, so he said: Do not drink from its milk except what is left over from its offspring. Then when the day of sacrifice comes, slaughter it and its offspring. His statement: Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House means the place of the offering and its end at the Ancient House, which is the Kaaba, as God Almighty said: An offering reaching the Kaaba and He said: And the offering is bent so that it reaches its place. We have already discussed the meaning of the Ancient House a little while ago, and praise be to God. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ata’ who said: Ibn Abbas used to say: Whoever circumambulates the House has become free from the obligation. God Almighty said: Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.
22:34: God the Almighty informs that the ritual slaughtering and shedding of blood in the name of God has always been permissible in all religions. Ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And for every nation We have appointed a ritual, he said: a festival. Ikrimah said: a slaughter. Zaid bin Aslam said in his statement, And for every nation We have appointed a ritual, that it is Mecca, God has never appointed a ritual for any nation other than it. And His statement, That they may mention the name of God over the livestock that He has provided for them, as proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Anas, who said: Two horned white rams were brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said Bismillah and Takbir and placed his foot on their sides. Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Salam bin Maskeen told us on the authority of Aaidh God Al-Majashi'i on the authority of Abu Dawud - who is Nafi' bin Al-Harith - on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam, who said: I said or they said: O Messenger of God, what are these sacrifices? He said: The Sunnah of your father Abraham. They said: What do we have from it? He said: For every hair a good deed. He said: And for wool? He said: For every hair of wool a good deed. Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah included it in his Sunan on the authority of Salam bin Maskeen. And His statement: Your God is one God, so submit to Him means your deity is one, even though the laws of the prophets varied and some abrogated others, as they all call to the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him. And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him, ‘There is no god but Me, so worship Me’ That is why He said: So submit to Him meaning be sincere and submit to His rule and obedience. And give good tidings to the humble Mujahid said: the reassured. Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: the humble. As-Suddi said: the fearful. Amr ibn Aws said: the humble are those who do not wrong and do not retaliate when wronged. Ath-Thawri said: And give good tidings to the humble he said: the reassured, satisfied with the decree of God and submitting to Him. And it is better to interpret what follows it, which is His statement: Those whose hearts tremble when God is mentioned meaning their hearts fear Him and who are patient over what befalls them meaning of calamities. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: By God, we will be patient or we will be destroyed. And those who establish prayer The majority read it with the addition of the seven and the rest of the ten also. Ibn Al-Sameeq read And those who establish prayer in the accusative case. According to Al-Hasan Al-Basri: And those who establish prayer The nun was only deleted here for the sake of alleviation. If it had been deleted for the sake of the addition, prayer would have been in the accusative case, but for the sake of alleviation, so it was in the accusative case, meaning those who fulfill God’s right in what He has obligated upon them of performing His obligations. And from what We have provided them they spend meaning and they spend what God has given them of good provision on their families, slaves, poor and needy, and they do good to creation while maintaining God’s limits. This is unlike the characteristics of the hypocrites, for they are the opposite of all of this as explained in Surat Bara’ah.
