22:36: God Almighty says, thanking His servants for what He created for them of the bodies and made them from His symbols, which is that He made them to be offered as sacrifices to His Sacred House, rather it is the best of what is offered to Him, as God Almighty said: Do not violate the symbols of God, nor the sacred month, nor the offerings, nor the garlands, nor those who are at the Sacred House the verse, Ibn Jurayj said, Ata said in His statement: And the sacrificial animals We have made for you from the symbols of God he said the cow and the camel, and this is what was narrated from Ibn Umar, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and Mujahid said: The sacrificial animals are from the camels. I said As for applying the sacrificial animal to the camel, it is agreed upon, and they differed about the validity of applying the sacrificial animal to the cow in two opinions, the most correct of which is that it is applied to it in the Shari'ah as the hadith is authentic, then the majority of scholars are of the opinion that the sacrificial animal is sufficient for seven and the cow is sufficient for seven, as was proven by the hadith in Muslim from the narration of Jabir bin Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to share in the sacrificial animals the sacrificial animal On behalf of seven, and a cow on behalf of seven. Ishaq bin Rahawayh and others said: Rather, a cow and a camel are sufficient on behalf of ten. A hadith on this was reported in Musnad al-Imam Ahmad, Sunan al-Nasa’i and others, and God knows best. And his saying: There is good for you in it means reward in the Hereafter. On the authority of Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Ka’bi, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No action done by the son of Adam on the Day of Sacrifice is more beloved to God than shedding blood. And it will come on the Day of Resurrection with its horns, hooves and hair, and the blood will fall in a place with God before it falls to the ground, so be content with it.” Narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi, who classed it as hasan. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Abu Hazim used to borrow and drive the sacrificial animals. It was said to him: Do you borrow and drive the sacrificial animals? He said: I heard God say to you: There is good for you in it. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have not spent silver on anything better than slaughtering it on the day of Eid. Narrated by al-Daraqutni in his Sunan. Mujahid said: There is good for you in it means reward and benefits. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: He rides it and milks it when he needs it. And his saying: Then mention the name of God over them, while they are in line. And on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abdullah bin Hantab, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: “I prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the Eid al-Adha. When he finished, a ram was brought and he slaughtered it, and he said: ‘In the name of God and God is the greatest. O God, this is on my behalf and on behalf of those of my nation who did not sacrifice.’” Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two rams on the day of Eid, and when he turned them, he said: ‘I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, a monotheist, a Muslim, and I am not of those who associate others with God. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds, He has no partner. This is what I have been commanded to do, and I am the first of the Muslims. O God, from You and for You, on behalf of Muhammad and his nation. Then he mentioned the name of God, said Allahu Akbar and slaughtered.” On the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of Abu Rafi’, “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, offered a sacrifice, he would buy two fat, horned, white rams. When he prayed and preached to the people, one of them would be brought to him while he was standing in his prayer place, and he would slaughter it himself with a knife. Then he would say: ‘O God, this is on behalf of my entire nation: whoever testified to Your monotheism and testified to my conveyance.’ Then the other would be brought to him and he would slaughter it himself. Then he would say: ‘This is on behalf of Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.’ He would feed them both to the poor and he and his family would eat from them.” Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Majah. Al-A'mash said on the authority of Abu Thabyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: Then mention the name of God over it while standing, he said: Standing on three legs, with its left hand tied, saying: In the name of God, God is the Greatest, there is no god but God, O God, from You and for You. And similarly it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ali ibn Abi Talhah and Al-Awfi on the authority of Ibn Abbas something similar to this. And Laith said on the authority of Mujahid: If its left leg is tied, it stands on three. And Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated something similar on his authority. And Ad-Dahhak said: One leg is tied, so it stands on three. And in the two Sahihs on the authority of Ibn Umar that he came upon a man who had made his sacrificial animal kneel while he was slaughtering it, so he said: Send it standing, tied, the Sunnah of Abu Al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace. And on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions used to slaughter sacrificial animals while their left leg was tied, standing on what remained of their legs. Narrated by Abu Dawud. And Ibn Lahi'ah said: Ata' ibn Dinar told me that Salim ibn Abdullah said to Sulayman ibn Abdul Malik: Stand on its right side and slaughter on its left side. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir, describing the Farewell Pilgrimage, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered sixty-three camels with his own hand, and he began to stab them with a spear in his hand. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada who said: In the letter of Ibn Masoud, Sawaf means standing upright. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, whoever reads it as Sawafin said: Maqoolah, and whoever reads it as Sawaf said: She stands in rows before it. Tawus, al-Hasan and others said: So mention the name of God over it, standing upright meaning purely for God Almighty, and Malik narrated it likewise on the authority of al-Zuhri. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid said: Sawaf does not contain polytheism like the polytheism of the pre-Islamic era with their idols. And his saying: And when its sides have fallen down, Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: meaning it has fallen to the ground, and this is a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And this is what Muqatil ibn Hayyan said, and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And when its sides have fallen down, meaning it has been slaughtered. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: And when its sides have fallen down, meaning it has died. And this statement is what Ibn Abbas and Mujahid meant, because it is not permissible to eat from a sacrificial animal that has been slaughtered until it dies and its movement stops. It was reported in a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Do not hasten souls to perish. It was narrated by al-Thawri in his Jami’ on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Qarafisah al-Hanafi, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he said that. It is supported by the hadith of Shaddad ibn Aws in Sahih Muslim, “God has prescribed kindness in all things, so when you kill, kill in the best way, and when you slaughter, slaughter in the best way. Let each one of you sharpen his blade and let his slaughtered animal be comfortable.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Waqid al-Laythi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever is cut from an animal while it is alive is dead. Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it. And his saying: So eat from it and feed the contented and the needy. Some of the Salaf said: His saying: So eat from it is an order of permission. Malik said: It is recommended, and others said: It is obligatory, and this is a view of some Shafi’is. They differed about what is meant by the contented and the needy. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The contented is the one who is satisfied with what you give him while he is in his house, and the needy is the one who approaches you and touches you so that you give him meat without asking, and this is what Mujahid and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The contented is the one who is self-sufficient, and the needy is the one who asks, and this is the saying of Qatadah, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and Mujahid in a narration from him. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Zaid ibn Aslam, Ibn al-Kalbi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Malik ibn Anas said: The contented is the one who is content with you and asks you, and the needy is the one who approaches you humbly and does not ask you, and this is the wording of al-Hasan. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: The contented is the one who asks, and he said: Haven’t you heard the saying of al-Shamakh: A man's wealth makes him rich, but his poverty is more honorable than his contentment. He said: He is satisfied with asking, and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ibn Aslam said: The contented is the poor who goes around, and the needy is the friend and the weak who visits, and this is a narration from his son Abdullah bin Zayd also. And from Mujahid also: The contented is your rich neighbor who sees what enters your house, and the needy is the one who approaches you from the people, and from him: The contented is the greedy, and the needy is the one who approaches with his body, whether rich or poor, and from Ikrimah something similar, and from him: The contented is the people of Mecca, and Ibn Jarir chose that the contented is the beggar, because he is from the one who raised his hand to ask, and the needy is from the word I’tiraa which is the one who exposes himself to eating meat. And this noble verse was used as evidence by those scholars who believed that the sacrifice is divided into three parts: a third for its owner to eat, a third to give as a gift to his companions, and a third to be given in charity to the poor, because God the Almighty said: So eat from it and feed the contented and the needy. In the authentic hadith, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the al-Nas 114:I forbade you from storing the meat of the sacrificial animals for more than three days, so eat and save whatever you want. In another narration: Eat, save and give in charity. In another narration: Eat, feed others and give in charity. The second opinion is that the one who is sacrificing eats half and gives the other half in charity, based on the statement in the previous verse: Eat from it and feed the poor and needy, and based on the statement in the hadith: Eat, save and give in charity. If he eats all of it, it was said that he is not liable for anything, and Ibn Surayj from the Shafi’is said the same. Some of them said that he is liable for all of it in return for its like or its value. It was said that he is liable for half of it, and it was said that he is liable for a third of it. It was said that he is liable for the smallest part of it, and this is the well-known opinion of the Shafi’i school of thought. As for the hides, in Musnad Ahmad, on the authority of Qatada bin Al-Nu’man, in the hadith on sacrificial animals, Eat and give in charity, and enjoy their hides, but do not sell them. Some scholars have permitted selling them, and some of them have said: The price should be shared with the poor, and God knows best. Question On the authority of Al-Bara’ bin ‘Aazib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then we return and slaughter. Whoever does that has followed our Sunnah, and whoever slaughters before the prayer, it is only meat that he has presented to his family and it is not part of the ritual sacrifice at all.” Narrated by both of them. For this reason, Al-Shafi’i and a group of scholars said: The first time for slaughtering the sacrificial animals is when the sun rises on the Day of Sacrifice and the time for the Eid prayer and the two sermons has passed. Ahmad added: And the imam should slaughter after that, as it came in Sahih Muslim: And do not slaughter until the imam slaughters. Abu Hanifah said: As for the people of the villages of Sawad and the like, they may slaughter after dawn, as there is no Eid prayer prescribed for them. As for the people of the cities, they should not slaughter until the imam prays, and God knows best. Then it was said: It is not prescribed to slaughter except on the Day of Sacrifice alone. It was said: The Day of Sacrifice is for the people of the cities because sacrifices are easy for them. As for the people of the villages, it is the Day of Sacrifice and the Days of Tashreeq after it. This is what Saeed bin Jubair said. It was said: The Day of Sacrifice and the day after it are for everyone. It was said: And two days after it. This is what Imam Ahmad said. It was said: The Day of Sacrifice and the three Days of Tashreeq after it. This is what Al-Shafi’i said, based on the hadith of Jubair bin Mut’im that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All the Days of Tashreeq are for slaughtering. Narrated by Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. It was said: The time for slaughtering extends to the end of Dhul-Hijjah. This is what Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman said, and it is a strange statement. And His statement: Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful. God Almighty says for this reason We have subjected them to you, meaning We have tamed them for you, and made them obedient and submissive to you. If you wish, you may ride them, if you wish, you may milk them, and if you wish, you may slaughter them, as God Almighty said: “Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, so they own them? And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat. And they have in them benefits and drinks. So will they not be grateful?” And He said in this noble verse: Thus have We subjected them to you that you may be grateful.
22:37: God the Almighty says: The slaughtering of these gifts and sacrifices has only been prescribed for you so that you may remember Him when you slaughter them, for He is the Creator, the Provider. None of their meat or blood reaches Him, for He is the One who is independent of anything other than Him. When they slaughtered them for their gods in their time of ignorance, they would put some of the meat of their sacrifices on them and sprinkle some of their blood on them, so God the Almighty said: Their meat and their blood will not reach God. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Muhammad ibn Abi Hammad told us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mukhtar told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: The people of the time of ignorance used to sprinkle the Kaaba with camel meat and blood, so the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We are more deserving of sprinkling, so God revealed: Their meat and blood will not reach God, but it is your piety that reaches Him, meaning He accepts that and rewards for it, as stated in the Sahih: Indeed, God does not look at your forms or your colors, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds. It was mentioned in the hadith: Charity falls into the hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the beggar, and blood falls to a place with God before it falls to the ground, as mentioned in the hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Majah and al-Tirmidhi, and he authenticated it on the authority of Aisha, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Its meaning is that it was brought to ensure acceptance by God for whoever is sincere in his work, and it has no meaning that comes to mind for the investigating scholars other than this, and God knows best. Waki` said on the authority of Yahya bin Muslim Abu Ad-Dahhak: I asked `Amir Ash-Sha`bi about the hides of sacrificial animals, and he said: Neither their meat nor their blood shall reach God. If you wish, then sell, and if you wish, then keep, and if you wish, then give in charity. And His statement, Thus has He subjected them to you, means for this reason He subjected the bodies to you, that you may glorify God for having guided you, meaning that you may magnify Him as He has guided you to His religion and law and what He loves and is pleased with, and He has forbidden you from doing what He hates and rejects. And His statement, And give good tidings to the doers of good, means, give good tidings, O Muhammad, to the doers of good, that is, in their work, those who abide by the limits of God, who follow what the Messenger has prescribed for them, who believe in what he conveyed to them and brought to them from their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Question Abu Hanifa, Malik and al-Thawri held the view that the sacrifice is obligatory for whoever possesses the minimum amount of money. Abu Hanifa also added the condition of residence, and he cited as evidence for them what Ahmad and Ibn Majah narrated with a chain of transmission whose men are all trustworthy, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: Whoever finds means but does not sacrifice, should not come near our place of prayer. However, it is strange, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal denounced it. Ibn Umar said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, lived for ten years sacrificing. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi. Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad said: The sacrifice is not obligatory, rather it is recommended, based on what is stated in the hadith: There is no right on wealth except zakat. It was previously mentioned that the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, sacrificed on behalf of his ummah, so that dropped its obligation on them. Abu Sariha said: I was a neighbor of Abu Bakr and Umar, and they did not sacrifice for fear that people would follow their example. Some people said: The sacrifice is a communal Sunnah. If one person from a house, neighborhood, or household does it, the rest are exempted from it because the purpose is to display the symbol. Imam Ahmad and the Sunan scholars narrated, and at-Tirmidhi classed it as hasan, on the authority of Muhannaf ibn Sulaym that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say in Arafat: “Every household must offer a sacrifice and an ‘atirah every year. Do you know what ‘atirah is? It is what they call Rajabiyah.” He spoke about its chain of transmission. Abu Ayyub said: During the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), a man would sacrifice a single sheep on behalf of himself and his family, and they would eat and feed each other until he started showing off to people, and it became as you see. Narrated by at-Tirmidhi, who classed it as hasan, and by Ibn Majah. Abdullah ibn Hisham would sacrifice a single sheep on behalf of all his family. Narrated by al-Bukhari. As for the age of the sacrifice, Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not slaughter except an adult animal, unless it is difficult for you, then slaughter a young sheep. From here, Az-Zuhri believed that a young sheep is not sufficient, and Al-Awza’i opposed him and believed that a young sheep of any kind is sufficient, and they are both strange. The majority of scholars agree that a two-year-old camel, cow, or goat is sufficient, or a young sheep. As for a two-year-old camel, it is one that is five years old and has entered its sixth year. As for a cow, it is one that is two years old and has entered its third year, or it was said that it is three years old and has entered its fourth year. As for a young sheep, it was said that it is one year old, or ten months old, or eight, or six months old, which is the least that has been said about its age. Anything less than that is a lamb, and the difference between them is that the hair on the back of a lamb is standing, while the hair on the back of a young sheep is asleep. It has parted at the temples, and God knows best.
22:38: God Almighty informs us that He protects, guards, and grants victory to His servants who put their trust in Him and turn to Him, from the evil of the wicked and the plots of the wicked, as He Almighty said: Is not God sufficient for His servant? And He said: “And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose. God has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.” And His statement: Indeed, God does not like any treacherous ingrate, meaning that He does not like among His servants those who are characterized by this, which is treachery in covenants and agreements, not fulfilling what he said, and ingratitude is denying blessings, not acknowledging them.
22:39: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Muhammad and his companions when they were expelled from Mecca. Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and more than one of the early Muslims such as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, Zaid ibn Aslam, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Qatadah, and others said: This is the first verse revealed about jihad. Some of them used this verse as evidence that the surah is Madani. Ibn Jarir said: Yahya ibn Dawud Al-Wasiti told me, Ishaq ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Muslim, who is Al-Batin, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was expelled from Mecca, Abu Bakr said: They expelled their Prophet, to God we belong and to Him we shall return, so that he would perish. Ibn Abbas said: Then God, the Almighty, revealed: "Permission to fight has been given to those who are being fought, because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory." Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: Then I knew that there would be fighting. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of Ishaq ibn Yusuf Al-Azraq with this, and he added: Ibn Abbas said: It is the first verse revealed about fighting. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i in their Sunan interpretations, and by Ibn Abi Hatim from the hadith of Ishaq bin Yusuf. Al-Tirmidhi and Waki’ both added on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: A good hadith. It was narrated by more than one person on the authority of Al-Thawri, but Ibn Abbas is not included in it. And His statement: And indeed, God is able to give them victory means that He is able to give victory to His believing servants without fighting, but He wants His servants to exert their utmost effort in obeying Him, as He said: “So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike their necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds; then either grant them favor afterwards or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens. That is so. And if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but [He intends] to test some of you by means of others. And as for those who are killed in the way of God - never will He let their deeds perish. He will guide them and amend their condition. And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them.” And God, the Most High, said: “Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people. And He will remove the anger of their hearts. And God turns in mercy to whom He wills. And God is Knowing and Wise.” And He said: “Or do you think that you will be left while God has not yet known those among you who strive and have not taken as allies other than God or His Messenger or the believers? And God is Acquainted with what you do?” And He said: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet known those among you who strive and have not taken as allies other than God or His Messenger or the believers? And God is Acquainted with what you do?” And He said: “Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet known those among you who strive and have not yet known The patient ones. He said: “And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive among you [for the cause of God] and the patient, and We will make evident [what is] your report.” There are many verses on this. That is why Ibn Abbas said in his statement: And indeed, God is able to give them victory, and He did. Rather, the Almighty legislated jihad at the most appropriate time for it, because when they were in Mecca, the polytheists were more numerous, so if He had ordered the Muslims, who were less than a tenth, to fight the rest, it would have been difficult for them. That is why when the people of Yathrib pledged allegiance on the night of Al-Aqaba to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were more than eighty in number. They said: O Messenger of God, should we not attack the people of the valley, meaning the people of Mina, during the nights of Mina and kill them? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have not been commanded to do this. So when the polytheists rebelled and expelled the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among them and intended to kill him, and scattered his companions in scatter, a group of them went to Abyssinia and others to Medina. When they settled in Medina and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met them and they gathered around him and supported him and it became a house of Islam and a stronghold to which they could take refuge, God prescribed jihad against the enemies. This verse was the first to be revealed regarding that. God, the Most High, said: “Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought against because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory. * Those who have been expelled from their homes without right.” Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They were expelled from Mecca to Medina without right, meaning Muhammad and his companions, except that they say, ‘Our Lord is God.’ That is, they had not done any harm to their people, nor had they committed any sin. However, they believed in the Oneness of God and worshipped Him without any partner, and this is an exception in relation to what is in the same matter. As for the polytheists, it is the greatest of sins, as God Almighty said: They expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord. And God Almighty said in the story of the People of the Trench: And they did not resent them except because they believed in God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. And for this reason, when the Muslims were chanting in the construction of the trench and saying: O God, if it were not for you, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. So send down tranquility upon us and plant firmly our feet if we meet [the enemy]. Those who have transgressed against us, if they wanted to cause discord, we would refuse. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) agreed with them and said with them at the end of each rhyme. So when they said: If they wanted to cause strife, we refused, he said: We refused, extending his voice. Then God the Almighty said: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, meaning, had He not repelled some people from others, and prevented the evils of some people from others through the causes He creates and decrees, the earth would have been corrupted and the strong would have destroyed the weak. The monasteries would have been demolished, which are the small temples of the monks, said Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Abu al-Aaliyah, Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, and others. Qatada said: They are the temples of the Sabians, and in a narration from him: the monasteries of the Magians. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They are the houses on the roads, and churches, which are larger than them, and have more worshippers in them, and they are also for the Christians, said Abu al-Aaliyah, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Sakhr, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, Khasif, and others. Ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Mujahid and others that they are the churches of the Jews. Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they are the churches of the Jews. Mujahid only said: They are the churches, and God knows best. And his saying: And prayers Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The prayers are the churches. And Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said the same: They are the churches of the Jews, and they call them prayers. Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of someone who told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas that they are the churches of the Christians. Abu Al-Aaliyah and others said: The prayers are the temples of the Sabians. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: The prayers are mosques for the People of the Book and the Muslims on the roads, as for the mosques, they are for the Muslims. And his saying: The name of God is mentioned therein much it was said: The pronoun in his saying The name of God is mentioned therein much refers to the mosques because they are the closest of the things mentioned. Ad-Dahhak said: All of them are where the name of God is mentioned much. Ibn Jarir said: The correct thing is to demolish the monasteries of the monks and the churches of the Christians and the prayers of the Jews, which are their churches, and the mosques of the Muslims in which the name of God is mentioned much, because this is what is commonly used in the speech of the Arabs. Some scholars said: This is a progression from the least to the most until it ends with the mosques, which are more populated and have more worshippers, and they are the ones with the correct intention. And His statement: And God will surely support those who support Him is like His statement, the Most High: “O you who have believed, if you support God, He will support you and plant firmly your feet. And as for those who disbelieve - then wretched is theirs, and He will render their deeds worthless.” And His statement, Indeed, God is Strong and Exalted in Might describes Himself with strength and might, for by His strength He created everything and determined it with a measure, and by His might no one can subdue Him nor can any victor overcome Him, rather everything is humble before Him and is in need of Him. And whoever the Strong and Exalted supports, he is the victorious, and his enemy is the vanquished. God the Most High said: “And Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they will be the victorious. And indeed, Our soldiers will be the predominant.” And God the Most High said: “God has decreed, ‘I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. Indeed, God is Strong and Exalted in Might.’” God the Almighty mentions His blessings upon His servants in what He has subjected to them of the sea that the ships may sail by His command. For He is the One who commanded the sea to carry them and that you may seek of His bounty that is, in trade and earnings and that you may be grateful that is, for obtaining the benefits brought from distant regions. Then the Almighty said: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth that is, of the planets, mountains, seas, and rivers, and everything that you benefit from, that is, all from His bounty, kindness, and grace. For this reason, He said: all from Him that is, from Him alone, with no partner in that, as the Almighty said: And whatever blessing you have is from God; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help. Ibn Jarir narrated, via Al-Awfi, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that God the Almighty said: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth—all from Him everything is from God. That name contains one of His names, so all of that is from Him and no one disputes it, and it was confirmed that it is thus. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani told us, al-Faryabi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Araka, who said: A man asked Abdullah ibn Amr may God be pleased with them both: From what did He create creation? He said: From light, fire, darkness, and dust. He said: Go to Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both and ask him. So he went to him and said the same thing to him. Ibn Abbas said: Go back to Him and ask Him from what He created all of that. So he went back to him and asked him, and he recited: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him. This is a strange narration and it contains something objectionable: Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought. God the Almighty says: Tell those who have believed to forgive those who do not expect the days of God. That is, to pardon them and endure the harm from them. This was at the beginning of Islam. They were commanded to be patient in the face of the harm caused by the polytheists and the People of the Book so that this would be a way to win them over. Then, when they persisted in their stubbornness, God prescribed fighting and jihad for the believers. This is how it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and Qatadah. Mujahid said: not expecting the days of God means they will not attain God's blessings. God the Almighty says: That He may reward a people for what they used to earn. That is, if you pardon them in this world, then God the Almighty will reward them for your bad deeds in the Hereafter. For this reason, God the Almighty says: "Whoever does righteousness does so for [his own] soul; and whoever does evil does so against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned." That is, you will return to Him on the Day of Resurrection and present your deeds to Him, and He will reward you for the good and the bad. And God the Almighty knows best.

22:41: Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu al-Rabi' al-Zahrani told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us on the authority of Ayoub and Hisham on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Uthman ibn Affan said: Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer and give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong was revealed about us. So we were expelled from our homes unjustly, except that we said: Our Lord is God. Then He established us in the land, so we established prayer and gave zakat, enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. And to God belongs the outcome of matters, so it is for me and my companions." Abu al-Aaliyah said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Sabah ibn Sawadah al-Kindi said: I heard Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz delivering a sermon and he said: "Those who, if We establish them in the land" the verse, then he said: Beware, it is not only for the ruler, but it is for the ruler and the one he governs. Shall I not inform you of what you have from the ruler in that regard, and what the ruler has from you in it? The ruler has the right to hold you accountable for the rights God has given you, to take from some of you what is due from others, and to guide you to that which is most upright as much as he can. You have the right to obey, neither forcefully nor under duress, nor in secret or in public. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: This verse is like His statement: God has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth Al-Anfal 1:17. His statement: And to God belongs the outcome of all matters is like His statement: And the [best] outcome is for the righteous. Zayd ibn Aslam said: And to God belongs the outcome of all matters Al-Anfal 1:17. And with God is the reward for what they did.
22:42: God Almighty says, consoling His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in denying those of his people who opposed him: “And if they deny you, then before them were denied the people of Noah, ‘Aad, and Thamud, and the people of Abraham, and the people of Lot, and the companions of Midian. And Moses denied.” That is, despite the clear signs and evident proofs he brought, So I granted respite to the disbelievers. That is, I gave them respite and delayed them, “Then I seized them. How was My denial?” That is, how was My denial of them and My punishment of them?! Some of the early Muslims mentioned that there were forty years between Pharaoh’s saying to his al-Nas 114:I am your supreme lord, and God’s destruction of him. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Abu Musa, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then he recited: “And such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” Then God Almighty said: How many a town have We destroyed while they were wrongdoers, meaning, they denied their messengers. And they lay desolate upon their roofs, Ad-Dahhak said: their roofs, meaning their buildings were ruined and their infrastructure was neglected. And a well that was abandoned, meaning, no water was drawn from it, and no one came to it despite the large number of people who came to it and the crowding around it. 22:47: God the Almighty says to His Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: And they urge you to hasten the punishment meaning these infidel atheists who deny God, His Book, His Messenger, and the Last Day, as God the Almighty says: And when they said, 'O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment' "And they said, 'Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning'". And His statement: "And God will not fail in His promise" meaning what He has promised of establishing the Hour, taking revenge on His enemies, and honoring His friends. Al-Asma'i said: I was with Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', when Amr ibn Ubayd came to him and said: O Abu Amr, does God fail in His promise? He said: No. Then he mentioned a verse of threat, and he said to him: Are you from the Persians? The Arabs consider going back on a promise to be meanness, and going back on a threat to be generosity. Haven't you heard the poet say: My power will frighten my cousin and neighbor, and I will not be deterred by the power of the threatening one. Even if I threatened him or promised him, I will break my promise and fulfill my promise. - And His statement: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. That is, He, the Most High, is not hasty, for the amount of a thousand years with His creation is like one day with Him in comparison to His forbearance, because He knows that He is able to take revenge, and that nothing escapes Him, even if He delays, waits, and gives hope. For this reason He said after this: And how many a town was I granted respite while it was unjust, then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Abda ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The poor Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day, five hundred years. And Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Al-Thawri on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr with it, and Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan Sahih. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission ending with him, saying: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, Saeed al-Jariri told us, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Sameer ibn Nahar, who said: Abu Hurairah said: The poor Muslims will enter Paradise before the rich by half a day. I said: How much is half a day? He said: Do you not read the Qur’an? I said: Yes. He said: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. Abu Dawud said at the end of the Book of the Epics of his Sunan: Amr ibn Uthman told us, Abu al-Mughira told us, Safwan told us, on the authority of Shuraih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I hope that my nation will not be unable to face their Lord by delaying them for half a day. It was said to Sa`d: What is half a day? He said: Five hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Isra`il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. He said: Of the days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Bishr, on the authority of Ibn al-Mahdi, and Mujahid and Ikrimah said the same. Ahmad ibn Hanbal stated it explicitly in his book, Al-Radd `ala al-Jahmiyyah. Mujahid said: This verse is like His statement: “He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth. Then it will ascend to Him in a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Arim Muhammad ibn al-Fadl told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Atiq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of a man from the People of the Book who converted to Islam, who said: God Almighty created the heavens and the earth in six days, And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. And He made the life span of the world six days, and He made the Hour on the seventh day, And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. So the six days have passed and you are on the seventh day, so the example of that is like that of a pregnant woman who enters her month, so at any moment she gives birth it is complete.

That is, God has sent me to you as a warner to you, before a severe punishment, and I have no say in your reckoning. Your affair is up to God. If He wills, He will hasten the punishment for you, and if He wills, He will delay it for you. If He wills, He will accept the repentance of those who repent to Him, and if He wills, He will lead astray those for whom He has decreed misery. He is the Doer of whatever He wills, desires, and chooses. There is no adjuster of His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. "I am only a clear warner to you. * So those who believe and do righteous deeds.' That is, their hearts believe and their faith is true to their deeds, for them is forgiveness and a noble provision." That is, forgiveness for their past bad deeds, and a good reward for the little of their good deeds. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: If you hear God the Almighty say, "and a noble provision," it means Paradise. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Habib told us, Abu Dawud told us, Shu'bah told us on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited An-Najm in Mecca, and when he reached this place: "Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-'Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other?" He said: Satan put on his tongue those exalted cranes and that their intercession is hoped for. They said: He did not mention our gods with goodness before today. So he prostrated and they prostrated, and God, the Almighty, revealed this verse: "And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech. But God nullifies that which Satan casts. Then God confirms His verses. And God is Knowing and Wise." It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Ghandar on the authority of Shu’bah in a similar manner, and it is mursal. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Yusuf ibn Hammad on the authority of Umayyah ibn Khalid on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Abu Bishr on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, as I think there is doubt in the hadith, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat al-Najm in Mecca until he reached Have you considered al-Lat and al-’Uzza? and he mentioned the rest of it. Then al-Bazzar said: We do not know of it being narrated in a continuous chain of transmission except with this chain of transmission. Umayyah ibn Khalid was the only one who connected it, and he is a well-known trustworthy person. Rather, this is narrated by way of al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu al-’Aliyah and al-Suddi in a mursal chain of transmission. Ibn Jarir also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and Muhammad ibn Qays in a mursal chain of transmission as well. Qatada said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying at the station when he dozed off, and Satan put on his tongue: And her intercession is hoped for, and she is with the high cranes, so the polytheists memorized it and Satan made it appear that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had recited it: And your tongues were humbled by it, so God revealed: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet, the verse, so God defeated Satan. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Musa bin Abi Musa al-Kufi told us, Muhammad bin Ishaq al-Musaybi told us, Muhammad bin Falih told us on the authority of Musa bin Uqbah on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Surat al-Najm was revealed and the polytheists used to say: If this man spoke well of our gods, we would approve of him and his companions, but he did not mention those who opposed his religion from the Jews and Christians with the same insults and evil that he mentioned about our gods. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was greatly distressed by what he and his companions suffered from their harm and denial, and he was saddened by their misguidance, so he wished for their guidance. So when God revealed Surat al-Najm He said: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? Is it for you the male and for Him the female? Satan then cast words at her when God mentioned the tyrants, saying: And indeed, they are for them the exalted cranes, and indeed, their intercession is that which is hoped for. This was from Satan’s rhyming and temptation, so these two words fell into the heart of every polytheist in Mecca and their tongues were humbled by them, and they rejoiced at them, and they said: Indeed, Muhammad has returned to his first religion and the religion of his people. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached the end of An-Najm, he prostrated, and everyone who was present with him, Muslim or polytheist, prostrated, except for Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, who was an old man, so he raised some dirt to his hand and prostrated on it, so both groups were amazed at their congregation in prostration to the prostration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for the Muslims, they were amazed at the prostration of the polytheists with them without faith or certainty, and the Muslims had not heard the verse that Satan cast into the ears of the polytheists, so their souls were reassured by what Satan cast into the wish of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Satan told them about it that The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had recited it in the Surah, so they prostrated themselves to glorify their gods. That word spread among the people, and Satan made it apparent until it reached the land of Abyssinia and the Muslims there, Uthman ibn Mazun and his companions. They said that all the people of Mecca had converted to Islam and prayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were informed of Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira’s prostration on the dust on his palm, and they said that the Muslims had believed in Mecca, so they came quickly. God abrogated what Satan had suggested and established His verses and protected him from slander. God said: “And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech. Then God abrogates what Satan casts into his speech. Then God establishes His verses. And God is Knowing and Wise. That He may make what Satan casts into a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.” So when God made clear His judgment and cleared him of Satan’s rhyme, the polytheists turned against the Muslims with their misguidance and enmity, and they became severe against them. This is also a mursal. In the interpretation of Ibn Jarir, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, something similar. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in his book, Dala’il Al-Nubuwwah, but Musa bin Uqbah did not permit it. He narrated it from his campaigns in a similar manner. He said: We have narrated this story on the authority of Abu Ishaq. I said, and Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned it in the biography in a similar manner. All of them are mursal and interrupted narrations, and God knows best. Al-Baghawi narrated it in his interpretation from a group of the words of Ibn Abbas, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and others in a similar manner. Then he asked a question here: How did something like this happen with the infallibility guaranteed by God Almighty for His Messenger, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him? Then he narrated answers from the people, the most subtle of which is that Satan made the polytheists hear that, so they thought that it came from the Messenger of God, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, but it was not so in reality. Rather, it was the work of Satan, not from the Messenger of God, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him. And God knows best. Thus, the answers of the theologians varied regarding this, estimating its authenticity. Judge Iyad, may God have mercy on him, addressed this in his book Al-Shifa’, and answered in summary that it is so because it is proven. And his saying: Except when he wishes, Satan casts into his wish This is a consolation from God to His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, meaning do not let that guide you, for the same happened to the messengers and prophets before you. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abbas said: In his wish if he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, so God nullifies what Satan casts, Then God confirms His verses. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If he wishes, Satan cast into his wish meaning: if he spoke, Satan cast into his speech. Mujahid said: If he wishes means if he said, and it is said that his wish was his recitation, Except for wishes they say but do not write. Al-Baghawi and most of the commentators said: The meaning of his saying: He wished is that he recited and read the Book of God, Satan cast into his wish meaning in his recitation. The poet said about Uthman when he was killed: Wishing for the Book of God the first night and the last one will meet the dove of destiny Ad-Dahhak said: If he wishes if he recites. Ibn Jarir said: This statement is more similar to the interpretation of the speech. His statement, Then God abrogates what Satan casts the true meaning of abrogation in the language is removal and lifting. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That is, God, the Most High, nullifies what Satan casts. Ad-Dahhak said: Gabriel abrogates by God’s command what Satan casts, and God perfected His verses. His statement, And God is Knowing means of what will happen of matters and events; nothing is hidden from Him. Wise means in His estimation, creation, and command. He has complete wisdom and a conclusive proof. That is why He said, That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt, polytheism, disbelief, and hypocrisy, like the polytheists when they rejoiced at that and believed that it was true from God, but it was from Satan. Ibn Jurayj said: Those in whose hearts is disease are the hypocrites, and those whose hearts are hardened are the polytheists. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: They are the Jews. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissent, meaning in error, opposition, and stubbornness far from the truth and right. And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, meaning that those who have been given beneficial knowledge by which they can differentiate between truth and falsehood and the believers in God and His Messenger may know that what We have revealed to you is the truth from your Lord who sent it down with His knowledge and preserved it, and guarded it from being mixed with it or anything else. Rather, it is a wise book. Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, sent down by One Full of Wisdom, Worthy of Praise. And His statement: So they believe in him means they believe him and submit to him, so their hearts submit to him meaning their hearts are humbled and submissive to him, And indeed, God guides those who believe to a straight path meaning in this world and the hereafter. As for in this world, He guides them to the truth and following it and enables them to oppose falsehood and avoid it, and in the hereafter He guides them to the straight path that leads to the levels of Paradise, and He removes them from painful torment and the lowest levels.

Then God establishes His verses. And God is Knowing and Wise. That He may make what Satan casts into a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and whose hearts are hardened. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.” So when God made clear His judgment and cleared him of Satan’s rhyme, the polytheists turned against the Muslims with their misguidance and enmity, and they became severe against them. This is also a mursal. In the interpretation of Ibn Jarir, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdul Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, something similar. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in his book, Dala’il Al-Nubuwwah, but Musa bin Uqbah did not permit it. He narrated it from his campaigns in a similar manner. He said: We have narrated this story on the authority of Abu Ishaq. I said, and Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned it in the biography in a similar manner. All of them are mursal and interrupted narrations, and God knows best. Al-Baghawi narrated it in his interpretation from a group of the words of Ibn Abbas, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and others in a similar manner. Then he asked a question here: How did something like this happen with the infallibility guaranteed by God Almighty for His Messenger, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him? Then he narrated answers from the people, the most subtle of which is that Satan made the polytheists hear that, so they thought that it came from the Messenger of God, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, but it was not so in reality. Rather, it was the work of Satan, not from the Messenger of God, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him. And God knows best. Thus, the answers of the theologians varied regarding this, estimating its authenticity. Judge Iyad, may God have mercy on him, addressed this in his book Al-Shifa’, and answered in summary that it is so because it is proven. And his saying: Except when he wishes, Satan casts into his wish This is a consolation from God to His Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, meaning do not let that guide you, for the same happened to the messengers and prophets before you. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abbas said: In his wish if he spoke, Satan cast into his speech, so God nullifies what Satan casts, Then God confirms His verses. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: If he wishes, Satan cast into his wish meaning: if he spoke, Satan cast into his speech. Mujahid said: If he wishes means if he said, and it is said that his wish was his recitation, Except for wishes they say but do not write. Al-Baghawi and most of the commentators said: The meaning of his saying: He wished is that he recited and read the Book of God, Satan cast into his wish meaning in his recitation. The poet said about Uthman when he was killed: Wishing for the Book of God the first night and the last one will meet the dove of destiny Ad-Dahhak said: If he wishes if he recites. Ibn Jarir said: This statement is more similar to the interpretation of the speech. His statement, Then God abrogates what Satan casts the true meaning of abrogation in the language is removal and lifting. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That is, God, the Most High, nullifies what Satan casts. Ad-Dahhak said: Gabriel abrogates by God’s command what Satan casts, and God perfected His verses. His statement, And God is Knowing means of what will happen of matters and events; nothing is hidden from Him. Wise means in His estimation, creation, and command. He has complete wisdom and a conclusive proof. That is why He said, That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease meaning doubt, polytheism, disbelief, and hypocrisy, like the polytheists when they rejoiced at that and believed that it was true from God, but it was from Satan. Ibn Jurayj said: Those in whose hearts is disease are the hypocrites, and those whose hearts are hardened are the polytheists. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: They are the Jews. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissent, meaning in error, opposition, and stubbornness far from the truth and right. And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, meaning that those who have been given beneficial knowledge by which they can differentiate between truth and falsehood and the believers in God and His Messenger may know that what We have revealed to you is the truth from your Lord who sent it down with His knowledge and preserved it, and guarded it from being mixed with it or anything else. Rather, it is a wise book. Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it, sent down by One Full of Wisdom, Worthy of Praise. And His statement: So they believe in him means they believe him and submit to him, so their hearts submit to him meaning their hearts are humbled and submissive to him, And indeed, God guides those who believe to a straight path meaning in this world and the hereafter. As for in this world, He guides them to the truth and following it and enables them to oppose falsehood and avoid it, and in the hereafter He guides them to the straight path that leads to the levels of Paradise, and He removes them from painful torment and the lowest levels.
22:55: God the Almighty says, informing about the disbelievers that they are still in doubt, that is, in suspicion of this Qur’an. Ibn Jurayj said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Zayd said from it, that is, from what Satan suggested, until the Hour comes upon them suddenly. Mujahid said: Suddenly. Qatada said, Suddenly the command of God came upon the people, and God never takes a people except when they are drunk, deceived, and in a state of comfort. So do not be deceived by God, for none are deceived by God except the wicked people. And His statement, or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day, Mujahid said: Ubayy bin Ka’b said: It is the day of Badr, and this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Qatada, and more than one said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Ikrimah and Mujahid said in a narration from them: It is the Day of Resurrection, for it has no night. Ad-Dahhak and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same. This statement is correct, even though the Day of Badr was among what they were promised, but this is what is meant. That is why he said: The kingdom on that Day belongs to God, and He will judge between them, like his saying: Master of the Day of Judgment. And His statement: The sovereignty on that Day will belong to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers. “Then those who believed and did righteous deeds” meaning their hearts believed and believed in God and His Messenger and acted in accordance with what they knew, and their hearts, words and deeds were in agreement will be in the Gardens of Delight meaning they will have eternal delight that will not change, disappear or perish. But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs meaning their hearts disbelieved in the truth and denied it, and denied it and disobeyed the Messengers and were too arrogant to follow them. For those is a humiliating punishment meaning in response to their arrogance and turning away from the truth, like the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, those who are too arrogant to worship Me will enter Hell [rendered] humiliated.

22:58: The Almighty tells us about those who emigrate for the sake of God, seeking His pleasure and seeking what is with Him, and leaving their homelands, families and friends, and departing their country for the sake of God and His Messenger, and in support of the religion of God, and then they are killed, that is, in jihad, or die a natural death, that is, without fighting, on their beds, then they have obtained a great reward and beautiful praise, as the Almighty said: And whoever emigrates from his home for the sake of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon God. And His statement: That God may provide them with a good provision means that He will bestow upon them from His grace and provision from Paradise what will please their eyes. “And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased,” meaning Paradise, as the Most High said: But if he is among those brought near, there will be comfort and basil and a garden of delight. So He informed that he will obtain comfort, provision, and a garden of delight, as He said here: That God may provide them with a good provision. Then He said: “He will surely admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased. And indeed, God is Knowing,” meaning of those who migrate and strive in His cause and of those who deserve that. Forbearing, meaning He is forbearing, pardons, and forgives their sins, and expiates them for their migration to Him and their trust in Him. As for the one who was killed in the way of God, whether he was a migrant or not, he is alive with his Lord and is provided for, as God the Almighty said: “And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, and are provided for.” There are many hadiths on this, as mentioned above. As for the one who died in the way of God, whether he was a migrant or not, this noble verse, along with the authentic hadiths, includes the provision of sustenance for him and the great kindness of God towards him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadheeh told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Shuraih, on the authority of Ibn Al-Harith - meaning Abd Al-Karim - on the authority of Ibn Uqbah - meaning Abu Ubaidah bin Uqbah - he said: Shurahbil bin Al-Samat told us: Our stay and our stay in a fortress in the land of the Romans was prolonged, and Salman - meaning the Persian, may God be pleased with him - passed by me and said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever dies as a guard, God will give him the same reward, and provide him with provision, and he will be safe from the afflictions. And recite if you wish: ‘And those who have emigrated in the cause of God and were killed or died - God will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, God is the best of providers. He will surely admit them to an entrance with which they will be pleased. And indeed, God is Knowing and Forbearing.’” He also said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Zaid bin Bishr told us, Hammam told me that he heard Abu Qabil and Rabia bin Saif Al-Ma’afari say: We were in Rhodes and with us was Fadala bin Ubaid Al-Ansari, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Two funerals passed by, one of them was killed and the other was deceased. The people leaned towards the one killed, so Fadala said: Why do I see the people leaning towards this one and leaving this one? They said: This one was killed in the way of God. He said: By God, I do not care from which of the two graves I am raised. Listen to the Book of God, And those who emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died, until he reached the end of the verse. He also said: My father told us, Abdah bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Salaman bin Amir al-Shaibani told us that Abd al-Rahman bin Jahdam al-Khawlani told him that he attended Fadalah bin Ubaid at sea with two funerals, one of which was hit by a catapult, and the other died. Fadalah bin Ubaid sat by the grave of the deceased, and it was said to him: You left the martyr and did not sit by him? He said: I do not care in which of their two graves you are sent, for God says: And those who emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died - God will surely provide for them a good provision, the two verses. So what do you seek, O servant, when you enter a place that pleases you and are provided with a good provision? By God, I do not care in which of their two graves you are sent. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih informed me on the authority of Salaman ibn Amir, who said: Fadala was the emir of the quarters in Rhodes, and he went out with the funeral processions of two men, one of whom was killed and the other deceased, and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. And His statement: And whoever punishes with the equivalent of that with which he was punished al-Baqarah 2:177, Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Ibn Jarir mentioned that it was revealed about a group of the Companions who encountered a group of polytheists in the month of Muharram, so the Muslims urged them not to fight them in the sacred month, but the polytheists refused to do anything but fight them and rebelled against them, so the Muslims fought them and God gave them victory over them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forgiving.

22:61: God Almighty says, pointing out that He is the Creator who disposes of His creation as He wills, as He said: “Say, ‘O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will and take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and abase whom You will. In Your hand is all good. Indeed, You are over all things competent. You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night. You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without account.’” The meaning of His bringing the night into the day and the day into the night is that He brings one into the other and the other into the other. Sometimes the night is long and the day is short, as in winter, and sometimes the day is long and the night is short, as in summer. And His statement: And that God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing means He hears the words of His servants. He sees them, nothing is hidden from Him in their conditions, movements, and stillness. And when He explained that He is the One who controls existence, the Ruler whose rule cannot be challenged, He said: That is because God is the Truth meaning the True God to whom worship is due, because He is the Possessor of the Great Authority, whatever He wills is, and whatever He does not will is not, and everything is in need of Him and humble before Him. And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood meaning of idols, rivals, and statues, and everything that is worshipped besides Him is falsehood, because He does not possess the power to harm or benefit. And His saying: And that God is the Most High, the Great is like He said, And He is the Most High, the Great and He said, The Great, the Most High so everything is under His power, authority, and greatness. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him, because He is the Great, than whom there is none greater, the Most High, than whom there is none higher, the Great, than whom there is none greater. He is exalted, sanctified, and far removed from what the unjust, aggressive people say, with a great exaltation.

And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood meaning of idols, rivals, and statues, and everything that is worshipped besides Him is falsehood, because He does not possess the power to harm or benefit. And His saying: And that God is the Most High, the Great is like He said, And He is the Most High, the Great and He said, The Great, the Most High so everything is under His power, authority, and greatness. There is no god but Him, and there is no lord but Him, because He is the Great, than whom there is none greater, the Most High, than whom there is none higher, the Great, than whom there is none greater. He is exalted, sanctified, and far removed from what the unjust, aggressive people say, with a great exaltation.
22:63: This is also evidence of His power and great authority, for He sends winds that stir up clouds and rains on barren land that has no vegetation, and it is lifeless, dry, black and barren. Then when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells. And His statement, Then the earth becomes green, the fa here is for succession, and the succession of each thing is according to its nature, as God the Almighty said, Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, and We made the clot into a lump of flesh, the verse. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that between every two things there are forty days, and despite this it is followed by the fa, and likewise here He said, Then the earth becomes green, meaning green after its dryness and transformation. It has been mentioned from some of the people of Hijaz that it becomes green after the rain, and God knows best. And His saying: Indeed, God is Kind and Aware means He is All-Knowing of what is in the corners, regions, and parts of the earth of grain, no matter how small, and nothing is hidden from Him. He delivers to each of them its share of water and it causes it to grow, as Luqman said: “O my son, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and be in a rock or in the heavens or in the earth, God will bring it forth. Indeed, God is Kind and Aware.” And He said: That they should not prostrate to God, Who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. And the Most High said: “Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is in a clear register.” And He said: And there is not hidden from your Lord, not an atom’s weight, on the earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or larger, but that it is in a clear register. For this reason, Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt or Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl said in his poem: And tell him, who makes the grain grow in the soil? So that the grass sways and grows from it. And his love comes out of it in their heads, so in that are signs for whoever is aware. And His saying: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth means that He owns all things, and He is independent of anything other than Him, and everything that is poor in relation to Him is a servant to Him. And His saying: Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is on the earth meaning of animals, inanimate objects, crops, and fruits, as He said: And has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth - all from Him meaning from His kindness, grace, and favor. And the ships sail through the sea by His command meaning by His subjection and control, meaning in the stormy sea and the clashing waves the ships sail with their people with a good wind, gentleness, and slowness, so they carry in them whatever they want of trade, merchandise, and benefits from one country to another and from one country to another, and they bring what those have to those, just as they went with what those have to those of what they need, seek, and want. And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission meaning if He willed, He would have permitted the sky to fall upon the earth and those in it would perish, but from His kindness, mercy, and power He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. That is why He said: Indeed, God “To mankind, Most Kind, Most Merciful, meaning with their injustice, as He said in the other verse: And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty. And His statement: “And it is He who gave you life, then will cause you to die, then will bring you back to life. Indeed, man is ungrateful.” Like His statement: How can you disbelieve in God when you were dead and He gave you life? Then He will cause you to die, then will bring you back to life, then to Him you will be returned. And His statement: Say, ‘God gives you life, then will cause you to die, then will gather you together for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.’ And His statement: They said, ‘Our Lord, You caused us to die twice, and You gave us life twice.’ The meaning of the statement is: How can you make rivals to God and worship other than Him, while He is independent in creation, provision, and control? And it is He who gave you life, meaning He created you after you were nothing worth mentioning, so He brought you into existence. Then He will cause you to die, then will bring you back to life, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, man is ungrateful, meaning ungrateful.

22:67: The Almighty informs us that He has made a ritual for every people. Ibn Jarir said: meaning that every nation has a prophet. He said: The origin of the ritual in the speech of the Arabs is the place that a person is accustomed to and visits either for good or evil. He said: This is why the rituals of Hajj were named that because people frequent them and devote themselves to them. If it is as he said that what is meant is that every nation has a prophet, We have made a ritual, then what is meant by His saying, So let them not dispute with you in the matter is these polytheists. If what is meant is that every nation has a ritual, We have made it a predestined decree, as He said: And for each is a direction toward which he turns. This is why He said here: They are its devotees, meaning those who do it. The pronoun here refers to those who have rituals and methods, meaning that these people only do this according to the decree and will of God, so do not be affected by their dispute with you and do not let that distract you from the truth that you are upon. This is why He said: “And invite to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight path.” This is a clear, straight path that leads to The intended meaning is, and this is like his saying: “And let not them turn you away from the verses of God after they have been revealed to you. And invite to your Lord.” And His statement: And if they argue with you, say, ‘God knows best what you do.’ is like His statement: “And if they deny you, then say, ‘To me is my work, and to you is your work. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do.’” And His statement: God knows best what you do is a severe threat and a definite warning, like His statement: “He is most knowing of what you conceal. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you.” That is why He said: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ. This is like His statement: Therefore, call upon God and be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their inclinations and say, ‘I believe in what God has revealed of the Book.’ verse.
